plain_english: Now, for its practical use, the sacrifice is first explained. In that context, initiation alone becomes the means for both enjoyment and liberation.
sanskrit_cite: athaitadupayogāya yāgastāvannirūpyate tatra dīkṣaiva bhoge ca muktau cāyātyupāyatām

plain_english: This works either by itself or through consecration, and its auxiliary aspect is now shown. Whoever desires enjoyments in a particular domain is appointed right there.
sanskrit_cite: svayaṃ saṃskārayogādvā tadaṅgaṃ tatpradarśyate yo yatrābhilaṣedbhogān sa tatraiva niyojitaḥ

plain_english: In the revered Svayambhuva scripture the Lord says that one attains success through mantra power. According to fitness, wherever a person's inclination lies, there he is placed.
sanskrit_cite: siddhibhāṅmantraśaktyeti śrīmatsvāyaṃbhuve vibhuḥ yogyatāvaśato yatra vāsanā yasya tatra saḥ

plain_english: He should be appointed so that he does not fall away. Thus, in the revered Malinimata, the teacher declared initiation to be a means for enjoyment and more, not for enjoyment alone.
sanskrit_cite: yojyo na cyavate tasmāditi śrīmālinīmate vadanbhogādyupāyatvaṃ dīkṣāyāḥ prāha no guruḥ

plain_english: Without initiation there is no eligibility for Shaiva yoga. And initiation does not bring about only eligibility for yoga.
sanskrit_cite: na cādhikāritā dīkṣāṃ vinā yoge@sti śāṅkare na ca yogādhikāritvamekamevānayā bhavet

plain_english: Through Shiva initiation one also gains eligibility for mantra and liberation. Thus, in this statement of the Malini, initiation is taught as a direct means to liberation.
sanskrit_cite: api mantrādhikāritvaṃ muktiśca śivadīkṣayā ityasminmālinīvākye sākṣānmokṣābhyupāyatā

plain_english: Earlier texts have spoken of initiation, and it is also said that, through consecration passed down in succession, initiation becomes a means to both liberation and enjoyment.
sanskrit_cite: dīkṣāyāḥ kathitā prācyagranthena punarucyate pāramparyeṇa saṃskṛtyā mokṣabhogābhyupāyatā

plain_english: For those who are determined but, due to incapacity, cannot take up knowledge, the teacher has declared this easier means as their procedure.
sanskrit_cite: yeṣāmadhyavasāyo@sti na vidyāṃ pratyaśaktitaḥ sukhopāyamidaṃ teṣāṃ vidhānamuditaṃ guroḥ

plain_english: Thus it is declared in the revered Matanga scripture as a means to liberation. For knowledge, whose nature is right understanding, is directly liberating.
sanskrit_cite: iti śrīmanmataṅgākhye hyuktā mokṣābhyupāyatā samyagjñānasvabhāvā hi vidyā sākṣādvimocikā

plain_english: It is clearly said there, in the knowledge section, in the discussion of the principles according to cause and effect and what is to be rejected or accepted.
sanskrit_cite: uktaṃ tatraiva tattvānāṃ kāryakāraṇabhāvataḥ heyādeyatvakathane vidyāpāda iti sphuṭam

plain_english: But for those who are incapable, initiation, conduct, and absorption are prescribed, and these should be preceded by knowledge. Therefore the knower is the most supreme.
sanskrit_cite: tatrāśaktāstu ye teṣāṃ dīkṣācaryāsamādhayaḥ te vidyāpūrvakā yasmāttasmājjñānyuttamottamaḥ

plain_english: Knowledge comes from scripture, and scripture is not to be heard by one who is uninitiated. Therefore initiation serves for him only as the consecration that makes this possible.
sanskrit_cite: jñānaṃ ca śāstrāttaccāpi śrāvyo nādīkṣito yataḥ ato@sya saṃskriyāmātropayogo dīkṣayā kṛtaḥ

plain_english: Wherever the teacher appoints him, he attains a fruit suited to his own understanding. This, it is said, was declared earlier regarding the knower.
sanskrit_cite: yatra tatrāstu guruṇā yojito@sau phalaṃ punaḥ svavijñānocitaṃ yāti jñānītyuktaṃ purā kila

plain_english: But if, by the Lord's grace, some divine fitness arises in both teacher and disciple, then initiation is of no use to them.
sanskrit_cite: yasya tvīśaprasādena divyā kācana yogyatā guroḥ śiśośca tau naiva prati dīkṣopayogitā

plain_english: Then knowledge itself is initiation, as explained in the revered Traisika. And for him there suddenly arises knowledge of the meaning of all the scriptures.
sanskrit_cite: jñānameva tadā dīkṣā śrītraiśikanirūpaṇāt sarvaśāstrārthavettṛtvamakasmāccāsya jāyate

plain_english: Thus, according to the teaching of the revered Malini, one who possesses innate awareness is the highest-qualified. Indeed, such a knower is regarded as a teacher.
sanskrit_cite: iti śrīmālinīnītyā yaḥ sāṃsiddhikasaṃvidaḥ sa uttamādhikārī syājjñānavānhi gururmataḥ

plain_english: Seeking benefit for himself or for others, he should contemplate this. By that statement in the Malini scripture, all of this has been made clear.
sanskrit_cite: ātmane vā parebhyo vā hitārthī cetayedidam ityuktyā mālinīśāstre tatsarvaṃ prakaṭīkṛtam

plain_english: Thus, in the injunction of the revered Kairana scripture, some are said to be fit for knowledge, others for conduct, others for initiation, and others for yoga.
sanskrit_cite: jñānayogyāstathā keciccaryāyogyāstathāpare dīkṣāyogyā yogayogyā iti śrīkairaṇe vidhau

plain_english: There, the one who has the stated marks, is skilled in action, yoga, and knowledge, and is elevated through successively higher levels, is declared to be the teacher.
sanskrit_cite: tatroktalakṣaṇaḥ karmayogajñānaviśāradaḥ uttarottaratābhūmyutkṛṣṭo gururudīritaḥ

plain_english: And that teacher, having examined or questioned the disciple who has been purified by the descent of any one of the powers mentioned before, should perform the rite of initiation.
sanskrit_cite: sa ca prāguktaśaktyanyatamapātapavitritam parīkṣya pṛṣṭvā vā śiṣyaṃ dīkṣākarma samācaret

plain_english: And it is said in the Svacchanda scripture that the teacher himself should ask the disciple: what fruit do you seek? I will begin the means suited to that.
sanskrit_cite: uktaṃ svacchandaśāstre ca śiṣyaṃ pṛcchedguruḥ svayam phalaṃ prārthayase yādṛktādṛksādhanamārabhe

plain_english: Because inclinations differ, attainment of the goal is impelled by mantra. In the offering, mantra, seal, path, and substances have a common use.
sanskrit_cite: vāsanābhedataḥ sādhyaprāptirmantrapracoditā mantramudrādhvadravyāṇāṃ home sādhāraṇā sthitiḥ

plain_english: Because inclinations differ, the fruits of disciples and of the teacher differ. The Shaiva practitioner is twofold: one whose way of life abandons worldly concerns.
sanskrit_cite: vāsanābhedato bhinnaṃ śiṣyāṇāṃ ca guroḥ phalam sādhako dvividhaḥ śaivadharmā lokojjhitasthitiḥ

plain_english: One type follows worldly duty, desires fruit, abides in what is good, and avoids what is evil. The seeker of liberation is twofold: the seedless one is free from pledges and the like.
sanskrit_cite: lokadharmī phalākāṃkṣī śubhasthaścāśubhojjhitaḥ dvidhā mumukṣurnirbījaḥ samayādivivarjitaḥ

plain_english: Another kind of candidate is like a child, a fool, an old person, a woman, an enjoyer, or someone sick. For such a person, the teaching of Shiva prescribes the seeded initiation.
sanskrit_cite: bālabāliśavṛddhastrībhogabhugvyādhitādikaḥ anyaḥ sabījo yasyetthaṃ dīkṣoktā śivaśāsane

plain_english: But for those who can endure the pairs of opposites, there is a seeded initiation made of pledges that confers grace. They must observe it, and they must also keep the special pledges.
sanskrit_cite: vidvaddvandvasahānāṃ tu sabījā samayātmikā dīkṣānugrāhikā pālyā viśeṣasamayāstu taiḥ

plain_english: For a desireless seeker of liberation, one should clearly contemplate the non-existence of past and future actions. But one should not do anything to remove the action that has already begun.
sanskrit_cite: abhāvaṃ bhāvayetsamyakkarmaṇāṃ prācyabhāvinām mumukṣornirapekṣasya prārabdhrekaṃ na śādhayet

plain_english: But for a practitioner who seeks power, one should purify in just that way. This initiation, grounded in Shiva-duty, takes away worldly duty.
sanskrit_cite: sādhakasya tu bhūtyarthamitthameva viśodhayet śivadharmiṇyasau dīkṣā lokadharmāpahāriṇī

plain_english: For those who remain in worldly duty, this initiation purifies only what is unrighteous, not what is auspicious. It is an initiation without mantra worship.
sanskrit_cite: adharmarūpiṇāmeva na śubhānāṃ tu śodhanam lokadharmiṇyasau dīkṣā mantrārādhanavarjitā

plain_english: When the body formed by already-begun karma falls away, this person enjoys powers such as aṇimā. After enjoying them, he goes onward to the level where he becomes joined, whether in the sakala state or in a limited condition.
sanskrit_cite: prārabdhadehabhede tu bhuṅkte@sāvaṇimādikam bhuktvordhvaṃ yāti yatraiṣa yukto@tha sakale@kale

plain_english: In the seedless initiation, one should purify the bond of pledge-conduct. Liberation can come through initiation alone, together with constant devotion to God and to the guru.
sanskrit_cite: samayācārapāśaṃ tu nirbījāyāṃ viśodhayet dīkṣāmātreṇa muktiḥ syādbhaktyā deve gurau sadā

plain_english: This seedless initiation is said to give immediate liberation, because it cuts away the three bonds of past, future, and already-begun karma.
sanskrit_cite: sadyonirvāṇadā seyaṃ nirbījā yeti bhaṇyate atītānāgatārabdhapāśatrayaviyojikā

plain_english: If a purified person gives up the body at the end of initiation, he reaches the supreme state. But if the body is given up in the case of seeded initiation, the result fails because karma is absent.
sanskrit_cite: dīkṣāvasāne śuddhasya dehatyāge paraṃ padam dehatyāge sabījāyāṃ karmābhāvādvipadyate

plain_english: The initiated person must always guard the bond of pledge-conduct. The guru himself should first ask, understand, and carefully examine the candidate.
sanskrit_cite: samayācārapāśaṃ tu dīkṣitaḥ pālayetsadā evaṃ pṛṣṭvā parijñāya vicārya ca guruḥ svayam

plain_english: When the guru wishes to give the right initiation, he should rely on the candidate's corresponding disposition. If the descent of grace has come to someone, the initiating guru, with regard to that initiation,
sanskrit_cite: ucitāṃ saṃvidhitsustāṃ vāsanāṃ tādṛśīṃ śrayet āyātaśaktipātasya dīkṣāṃ prati na daiśikaḥ

plain_english: must not show disrespect. This is established as the command of Shambhu. If the person is poor, the guru himself should perform the initiation using his own wealth.
sanskrit_cite: avajñāṃ vidadhīteti śaṃbhunājñā nirūpitā svadhanena daridrasya kuryāddīkṣāṃ guruḥ svayam

plain_english: A disciple may even beg for initiation with nothing more than durva grass and water. Or the disciple may first give to the guru wealth that is his own or that he has obtained by begging.
sanskrit_cite: api dūrvāmbubhiryadvā dīkṣāyai bhikṣate śiśuḥ bhikṣopāttaṃ nijaṃ vātha dhanaṃ prāggurave śiśuḥ

plain_english: By giving it, that wealth becomes purified and fit to be offered. In this matter, the first requirement is the entry into the freedom of the state of Shiva.
sanskrit_cite: dadyādyena viśuddhaṃ tadyāgayogyatvamaśnute tatrādau śivatāpattisvātantryāveśa eva yaḥ

plain_english: That person alone should be made the guru, for he is capable of giving initiation. His entry into the state of Shiva has been shown to come about through many means.
sanskrit_cite: sa eva hi guruḥ kāryastato@sau dīkṣaṇe kṣamaḥ śivatāveśitā cāsya bahūpāyā pradarśitā

plain_english: One gradual path takes an external form, using bathing, placement, worship, and similar acts. Among these many practices, one establishes the state of Shiva in the heart.
sanskrit_cite: kramikā bāhyarūpā tu snānanyāsārcanādibhiḥ bahvīṣu tāsu tāsveṣa kriyāsu śivatāṃ hṛdi

plain_english: By firmly establishing it, the clear-minded practitioner attains the state of Shiva. Having become Shiva, he undertakes to do whatever he wishes.
sanskrit_cite: saṃdadhaddṛḍhamabhyeti śivabhāvaṃ prasannadhīḥ śivībhūto yadyadicchettattatkartuṃ samīhate

plain_english: An external means identified with Shiva is not by itself what gives liberation. Liberation comes when teacher and disciple firmly hold the recognition: this is Shiva; I am indeed Shiva.
sanskrit_cite: śivābhimānitopāyo bāhyo heturna mokṣadaḥ śivo@yaṃ śiva evāsmītyevamācāryaśiṣyayoḥ

plain_english: For the two of them, firm identification, understood as cause and its bearer, is what liberates. The external does not succeed without the inner, and the inner does not succeed when cut off from the external.
sanskrit_cite: hetutadvattayā dārḍhyābhimāno mocako hyaṇoḥ nādhyātmena vinā bāhyaṃ nādhyātmaṃ bāhyavarjitam

plain_english: Success comes through knowledge and action together, and this paired principle shines forth. He established this by citing the revered Brahmayamala, where it says, 'O God...'
sanskrit_cite: siddhyejjñānakriyābhyāṃ taddvitīyaṃ saṃprakāśate śrībrahmayāmale deva iti tena nyarūpayat

plain_english: And in the revered Ananda scripture it is said that the wise person has no impurity. Rather, bathing and wearing good clothes serve to produce contentment.
sanskrit_cite: śrīmadānandaśāstre ca nāśuddhiḥ syādvipaścitaḥ kintu snānaṃ suvastratvaṃ tuṣṭisaṃjananaṃ bhavet

plain_english: There, through the familiar sequence of purifying the body and related measures, those who bathe can enter inwardly without effort. From that, purity arises.
sanskrit_cite: tatra prasiddhadehādimātṛnirmalatākramāt ayatnato@ntarantaḥ syānnairmalya snāyatāṃ tataḥ

plain_english: The bathing of the God of Gods is connected with what is called his eight forms. In that context, the true immersion is the inward plunging into the burning of impurity lit by mantra.
sanskrit_cite: snānaṃ ca devadevasya yanmūrtyaṣṭakamucyate tatraivaṃ mantradīpte@ntarmaladāhe nimajjanam

plain_english: There, centered in the heart of the chosen mantra, one should go and return three steps within the space of cow dust and perform the earthly bath. That bath gives steadiness.
sanskrit_cite: tatreṣṭamantrahṛdayo gorajo@ntaḥ padatrayam gatvāgatya bhajetsnānaṃ pārthivaṃ dhṛtidāyakam

plain_english: Having removed impurity with clay consecrated by the weapon mantra, one should then wash the body in order from head to feet with waters consecrated by the five-limb mantras.
sanskrit_cite: astramantritamṛddhūtamalaḥ pañcāṅgamantritaiḥ jalairmūrdhādipādāntaṃ kramādākṣālayettataḥ

plain_english: One should immerse while reciting the root mantra together with its limbs, or through becoming one with it. After rising, one should contemplate in the sky the sun that contains all the luminous deities.
sanskrit_cite: nimajjetsāṅgamūlākhyaṃ japannā tanmayatvataḥ utthāyāśeṣasajjyotirdevatāgarbhamambare

plain_english: With water and the Malini mantra, one should satisfy the sun, the satisfier of the whole world, and also satisfy the gods, ancestors, sages, yakshas, demons, and whatever else is elemental.
sanskrit_cite: sūryaṃ jalena mālinyā tarpayedviśvatarpakam devānpitṝnmunīnyakṣān rakṣāṃsyanyacca bhautikam

plain_english: One should satisfy all beings through the vital breath, whose nature is power, and that power is the sun. Then one should recite the single supreme mantra according to the method of utterance taught earlier.
sanskrit_cite: sarvaṃ saṃtarpayetprāṇo vīryātmā sa ca bhāskaraḥ tato japetparāmekāṃ prāguktoccārayogataḥ

plain_english: This is regarded as the water bath, culminating in the awareness of becoming one with that. For the fire bath, ash arisen from fire is recited over with the weapon mantra so that it removes impurity.
sanskrit_cite: ā tanmayatvasaṃvitterjalasnānamidaṃ matam agnyutthaṃ bhasma śastreṇa japtvā malanivarhaṇam

plain_english: Ash consecrated with the five-limb mantras is applied to the head, face, heart, and secret place. Then a handful of ash, recited over with the root mantra and its limbs, should be cast on the head.
sanskrit_cite: kavaktrahṛdguhyapade pañcāṅgairbhasma mantritam bhasmamuṣṭiṃ sāṅgamūlajaptāṃ mūrdhni kṣipettataḥ

plain_english: After washing the hands and feet with water alone, one performs sipping and the other acts, then satisfaction and recitation. In this way, the ash bath is indeed the fiery bath.
sanskrit_cite: hastapādau jalenaiva prakṣālyācamanādikam tarpaṇaṃ japa ityevaṃ bhasmasnānaṃ hi taijasam

plain_english: When a refreshing wind blows gently, like the dust raised by cows, one should perform the wind bath by uttering the mantra, or by moving back and forth in that wind.
sanskrit_cite: gorajovatyanudrikte vāyau hlādini mantravāk gatyāgatiprayoge vā vāyavyaṃ snānamācaret

plain_english: When one sits in the stainless sky with a gaze made one-pointed on the pervasive expanse, remembering the mantra, what other purity could there be beyond that?
sanskrit_cite: amale gagane vyāpinyekāgrībhūtadṛṣṭikaḥ smaranmantraṃ yadāsīta kānyā nirmalatā tataḥ

plain_english: Or, if one lets water falling from the stainless sky touch the body while joined with mantra recitation, that is such a sky bath.
sanskrit_cite: yadi vā nirmalādvyomnaḥ patatā vāriṇā tanum sparśayenmantrajapayuṅ nābhasaṃ snānamīdṛśam

plain_english: Thus, by contemplating with the state of Shiva in the lights of moon, sun, and fire, and by immersing purified through the Malini, where would one not become fit?
sanskrit_cite: evaṃ somārkatejaḥsu śivabhāvena bhāvanāt nimajjandhautamālinyaḥ kva vā yogyo na jāyate

plain_english: The self alone is the supreme lord, the great pool beyond ritual observance. Having immersed the universe there, one should abide in that very place as pure and as the purifier.
sanskrit_cite: ātmaiva parameśāno nirācāramahāhradaḥ viśvaṃ nimajjya tatraiva tiṣṭhecchuddhaśca śodhakaḥ

plain_english: Thus there is the group of eight baths, each later one better than the previous in purification. In every case, afterward one should apply that mantra in a unified form.
sanskrit_cite: iti snānāṣṭakaṃ śuddhāvuttarottaramuttamam sarvatra paścāttaṃ mantramekībhūtamupāharet

plain_english: The sage devoted to the eight baths attains in order firmness, nourishment, the burning away of impurity, power, pervasion, purification, abiding, and non-difference.
sanskrit_cite: ghṛtyāpyāyamalaploṣavīryavyāptimṛjisthitīḥ abhedaṃ ca kramādeti snānāṣṭakaparo muniḥ

plain_english: These eight forms are indeed gracious in nature and are essentially Shiva. Through meditation on them as one's own form and as Shiva's form, they grant their respective fruits.
sanskrit_cite: etā hyanugrahātmāno mūrtayo@ṣṭau śivātmikāḥ svarūpaśivarūpābhyāṃ dhyānāttattatphalapradāḥ

plain_english: By this method in worship, performing the application beginning with the bulb and the support, whether in expanded or condensed form, one obtains the corresponding fruit beginning with earth.
sanskrit_cite: anena vidhinārcāyāṃ kandādhārādiyojanām kurvanvyāsasamāsābhyāṃ dharādestatphalaṃ bhajet

plain_english: For in the movement of yoga, the mantras are earthly on earth, watery in water, and so on, until in Shiva they become wholly of Shiva's nature.
sanskrit_cite: tathāhi yogasaṃcāre mantrāḥ syurbhuvi pārthivāḥ āpye āpyā yāvadamī śive śivamayā iti

plain_english: In the revered Nirmaryada scripture this is well explained: earth and the other elements also have a special form approved by heroic practitioners.
sanskrit_cite: śrīnirmaryādaśāstre@pi taditthaṃ sunirūpitam dharādeśca viśeṣo@sti vīrasādhakasaṃmataḥ

plain_english: For heroic practitioners, battle dust is the heroic water, there is heroic ash and the great wind, and also the cremation ground, forest, and sky, along with the moon and sun as brought into that setting.
sanskrit_cite: raṇareṇurvīrajalaṃ vīrabhasma mahāmarut śmaśānāraṇyagaganaṃ candrārkau tadupāhitau

plain_english: The self, well established with all the affliction of conceptual thought shaken off, completes the heroic group of eight forms to be honored in bathing, worship, and so on.
sanskrit_cite: ātmā nirdhūtaniḥśeṣavikalpātaṅkasusthitaḥ snānārcādāvityupāsyaṃ vīrāṇāṃ vigrahāṣṭakam

plain_english: In the revered Mantrishiras it is taught that one may use wine, liquor, or other such spirits, provided they are very tasty, clear, subtle, and very fragrant.
sanskrit_cite: śrīmantriśirasi proktaṃ madyaśīdhusurādinā susvādunā prasannena tanunā susugandhinā

plain_english: Using the substance as present in the bulb and so on, within and without, one performs the five consecrations: inspection, sprinkling, striking, nourishing, and veiling.
sanskrit_cite: kandalādigatenāntarbahiḥ saṃskārapañcakam kṛtvā nirīkṣaṇaṃ prokṣya tāḍanāpyāyaguṇṭhanam

plain_english: In the middle of the mantra circle one performs worship and satisfaction with drops. With that substance one sprinkles oneself and performs consecratory sprinkling using the jar seal.
sanskrit_cite: mantracakrasya tanmadhye pūjāṃ vipruṭpratarpaṇam tenātmasekaḥ kalaśamudrayā cābhiṣecanam

plain_english: Through satisfaction of the deity, resting on the path of both body and vital breath, one obtains the fruit of all pilgrimages, austerities, sacrifices, gifts, and the like.
sanskrit_cite: devatātarpaṇaṃ dehaprāṇobhayapathāśritam sarvatīrthatapoyajñadānādi phalamaśnute

plain_english: In the wine bath, the foremost practitioner who seeks liberation may become liberated, because wine is of the nature of Śiva and all mantras arise from Śiva.
sanskrit_cite: madyasnāne sādhakendro mumukṣuḥ kevalībhavet yataḥ śivamayaṃ madyaṃ sarve mantrāḥ śivodbhavāḥ

plain_english: There is no difference between Śiva and Śakti; the rays arise from Śakti, and wine produces their bliss. Therefore wine is of the nature of Śiva.
sanskrit_cite: śivaśaktyorna bhedo@sti śaktyutthāstu marīcayaḥ tāsāmānandajanakaṃ madyaṃ śivamayaṃ tataḥ

plain_english: When the full form of consciousness is awakened, one is fit for ritual action. Bathing distinguished by mantra, meditation, and absorption is real bathing; what lacks that is not.
sanskrit_cite: prabuddhe saṃvidaḥ pūrṇe rūpe@dhikṛtibhājanam mantradhyānasamādhānabhedātsnānaṃ tu yanna tat

plain_english: Bathing is fitting because it brings fitness for nyāsa and other rites. This eightfold bathing is twofold, as outer and inner.
sanskrit_cite: yuktaṃ snānaṃ yato nyāsakarmādau yogyatāvaham asya snānāṣṭakasyāsti bāhyāntaratayā dvitā

plain_english: The inner bath is the flooding of nectar from the upper moon, established above the cranial aperture and pervading a span of one and a half finger-widths.
sanskrit_cite: āntaraṃ tadyathordhvendudhārāmṛtapariplavaḥ yato randhrordhvagāḥ sārdhamaṅgulaṃ vyāpya saṃsthitāḥ

plain_english: Eight forms are taught, each arising from the dvādaśānta. One may perform any one of these baths, or do them in two, three, or more ways.
sanskrit_cite: mūrtayo@ṣṭāvapi proktāḥ pratyekaṃ dvādaśāntataḥ eṣāmekatamaṃ snānaṃ kuryāddvitryādiśo@pivā

plain_english: Thus the rule of bathing has been declared by Bhairava for purification. Now what must be done after bathing is taught.
sanskrit_cite: iti snānavidhiḥ prokto bhairaveṇāmalīkṛtau snānānantarakartavyamathedamupadiśyate

plain_english: Seeing that one's inner state is clear, one should then go to the place of worship, such as a mountain top, a riverbank, a solitary liṅga, and so on.
sanskrit_cite: bhāvaṃ prasannamālocya vrajedyāgagṛhaṃ tataḥ parvatāgranadītīraikaliṅgādi yaducyate

plain_english: Those outer places are for particular attainments, not for liberation. The inner mountain-top and the like are within the body, approached through the application of prāṇa.
sanskrit_cite: tadbāhyamiha tatsiddhiviśeṣāya na muktaye ābhyantaraṃ nagāgrādi dehāntaḥ prāṇayojanam

plain_english: For practitioners this is a means to attainment, not to liberation. The pīṭha-place, however, is always fit for worship, as the scriptures declare.
sanskrit_cite: sādhakānāmupāyaḥ syātsiddhaye natu muktaye pīṭhasthānaṃ sadā yāgayogyaṃ śāstreṣu bhaṇyate

plain_english: That pīṭha, in its outer and inner form, is clearly present outside and in the body, because the Supreme Lord set it forth in the revered Naiśa Sañcāra.
sanskrit_cite: tacca bāhyāntarādrūpādbahirdehe ca susphuṭam yataḥ śrīnaiśasañcāre parameśo nyarūpayat

plain_english: His will is the supporting pīṭha in which all that moves and does not move is situated. That foremost pīṭha is Kāmarūpa, and from it comes the pair of bindu and nāda.
sanskrit_cite: tasyecchā pīṭhamādhāro yatrasthaṃ sacarācaram agryaṃ tatkāmarūpaṃ syādbindunādadvayaṃ tataḥ

plain_english: The nāda-pīṭha is Pūrṇagiri on the right, and on the left is the pīṭha Uḍḍayana. With bindu as the chief, this is the triad of pīṭhas.
sanskrit_cite: nādapīṭhaṃ pūrṇagirirdakṣiṇe vāmataḥ punaḥ pīṭhamuḍḍayanaṃ bindurmukhyaṃ pīṭhatrayaṃ tvidam

plain_english: One should know the half-pīṭha as having the form of conceptualization. Beyond that, in the śākta domain, Kuṇḍalinī and Vedakala belong to the triad of upapīṭhas.
sanskrit_cite: jñeyaṃ saṃkalpanārūpamardhapīṭhamataḥ param śāktaṃ kuṇḍalinī vedakalaṃ ca tryupapīṭhakam

plain_english: Devīkoṭṭa and Ujjayinī are two, and Kulagiri is another; Lālana, Baindava, and Vyāpti form the triad of saṃdohakas.
sanskrit_cite: devīkoṭṭojjayinyau dve tathā kulagiriḥ paraḥ lālanaṃ baindavaṃ vyāptiriti saṃdohakatrayam

plain_english: With Puṇḍravardhana, Vārendra, and likewise Ekāmra on the outside, the pīṭha is declared ninefold in an inner-outer sequence.
sanskrit_cite: puṇḍravardhanavārendre tathaikāmramidaṃ bahiḥ navadhā kathitaṃ pīṭhamantarbāhyakrameṇa tat

plain_english: Those who know the kṣetras speak of an eightfold group corresponding to the eight petals of the heart-lotus: Prayāga, Varaṇā, then Aṭṭahāsa, and Jayantikā.
sanskrit_cite: kṣetrāṣṭakaṃ kṣetravido hṛdambhojadalāṣṭakam prayāgo varaṇā paścādaṭṭahāso jayantikā

plain_english: Vārāṇasī, Kāliṅga, Kulūtā, and likewise Lāhulā belong to the eight upakṣetras, which they say correspond to the eight front petals of the heart-lotus.
sanskrit_cite: vārāṇasī ca kāliṅgaṃ kulūtā lāhulā tathā upakṣetrāṣṭakaṃ prāhurhṛtpadmāgradalāṣṭakam

plain_english: Viraja and Airuḍikā, Hālā, Elā, Pūḥ, Kṣīrikā, Purī, the place called Māyā, and Marudeśa are understood in both outer and inner form.
sanskrit_cite: virajairuḍikā hālā elā pūḥ kṣīrikā purī māyākhyā marudeśaśca bāhyābhyantararūpataḥ

plain_english: The eight upasaṃdohakas correspond to the junctions of the heart-lotus petals: Jālandhara, Naipāla, Kaśmīra, Gargikā, and Hara.
sanskrit_cite: hṛtpadmadalasandhīnāmupasaṃdohakāṣṭatā jālandharaṃ ca naipālaṃ kaśmīrā gargikā haraḥ

plain_english: There is also the site at the gate of the mleccha direction, Kurukṣetra, and Kheṭaka. A two-path junction arises, a three-path junction from the meeting of two, and further from the meeting of three.
sanskrit_cite: mlecchadigdvāravṛttiśca kurukṣetraṃ ca kheṭakam dvipathaṃ dvayasaṃghaṭṭāttripathaṃ trayamelakāt

plain_english: They hold that the four-path junction arises there itself by dissolution in the Śakti-bearing principle, and in this body it is established in the region of the nose, palate, and aperture.
sanskrit_cite: catuṣpathaṃ śaktimato layāttatraiva manvate nāsāntatālurandhrāntametaddehe vyavasthitam

plain_english: The middle triad is said to be the middle of the brows, the throat, and the heart. The navel, the bulb, and the abode of great bliss form the kaula triad.
sanskrit_cite: bhrūmadhyakaṇṭhahṛtsaṃjñaṃ madhyamaṃ tadudāhṛtam nābhikandamahānandadhāma tatkaulikaṃ trayam

plain_english: Mountain tops, riverbanks, and solitary liṅgas—why say more? All of that is in consciousness and present in prāṇa.
sanskrit_cite: parvatāgraṃ nadītīramekaliṅgaṃ tadeva ca kiṃ vātibahunā sarvaṃ saṃvittau prāṇagaṃ tataḥ

plain_english: Therefore worship should be situated in the body, taking the body as its abode. External worship, however, is for those who are skilled in the corresponding inner yoga path.
sanskrit_cite: tato dehasthitaṃ tasmāddehāyatanago bhavet bāhye tu tādṛśāntaḥsthayogamārgaviśāradāḥ

plain_english: The goddesses arise from their own nature, and the sacred seat is said to be external to that. This is like barbarians who, by their own nature, follow the path of unrighteousness.
sanskrit_cite: devyaḥ svabhāvājjāyante pīṭhaṃ tadvāhyamucyate yathā svabhāvato mlecchā adharmapathavartinaḥ

plain_english: In some such place, knowledge and yoga may be established by fixed rule, yet even one who is made of consciousness can fall into sinfulness through association with those there.
sanskrit_cite: tatra deśe niyatyetthaṃ jñānayogau sthitau kvacit yathācātanmayo@pyeti pāpitāṃ taiḥ samāgamāt

plain_english: Likewise, even one situated in a sacred seat attains fitness for knowledge, yoga, and the rest, primarily for one who sees inwardly in the body, in the breath, and in consciousness.
sanskrit_cite: tathā pīṭhasthito@pyeti jñānayogādipātratām mukhyatvena śarīre@ntaḥ prāṇe saṃvidi paśyataḥ

plain_english: This whole universe is already here, so what is the use of other outward displays of wandering? Thus, for those who seek the fruit of each respective circle, the matter applies both inwardly and outwardly.
sanskrit_cite: viśvametatkimanyaiḥ syādbahirbhramaṇaḍambaraiḥ ityevamantarbāhye ca tattaccakraphalārthinām

plain_english: The difference of sacred places is varied and, in scripture, beyond counting. In the Vīrāvalihṛdaya, seven places are mentioned, along with a pair of śakti-lotuses.
sanskrit_cite: sthānabhedo vicitraśca sa śāstre saṃkhyayojjhitaḥ śrīvīrāvalihṛdaye sapta sthānāni śaktikamalayugam

plain_english: Places such as the path of the gods, a crossroads, a cremation ground, a solitary spot, and an empty tree are taught as sites to be understood through etymology, quality, condition, and figurative meaning.
sanskrit_cite: surapathacatuṣpathākhyaśmaśānamekāntaśūnyavṛkṣau ca iti nirvacanaguṇasthityupacāradṛśā vibodha evoktaḥ

plain_english: Worship for liberation may take place in a circle established there, in the body, or externally; therefore no essential difference in the worship is to be made on the basis of place.
sanskrit_cite: tadadhiṣṭhite ca cakre śārīre bahiratho bhavedyāgaḥ muktaye tanna yāgasya sthānabhedaḥ prakalpyate

plain_english: This attainment does not operate by means of place, because it comes from the clarity of one's inner state; this is also said in the revered Nishacara for those who seek accomplishment.
sanskrit_cite: deśopāyā na sā yasmātsā hi bhāvaprasādataḥ uktaṃ ca śrīniśācāre siddhisādhanakāṅkṣiṇām

plain_english: One who seeks liberation should cast off attachment to place like a snake sheds its skin, because liberation is not produced by place; it comes when the truth reaches one's hearing.
sanskrit_cite: sthānaṃ mumukṣuṇā tyājyaṃ sarpakañcukavattvidam muktirna sthānajanitā yadā śrotrapathaṃ gatam

plain_english: When the truth of the guru is heard, liberation comes; worship then serves to strengthen it. Wherever the heart-lotus opens, that is where this awakening takes place.
sanskrit_cite: gurostattvaṃ tadā muktistaddārḍhyāya tu pūjanam yatra yatra hṛdambhojaṃ vikāsaṃ pratipadyate

plain_english: In that very inner abode, the glory of both outer and inner worship is established. Liberation does not come from going somewhere else; it comes from cutting the knot of ignorance.
sanskrit_cite: tatraiva dhāmni bāhye@ntaryāgaśrīḥ pratitiṣṭhati nānyatragatyā mokṣo@sti so@jñānagranthikartanāt

plain_english: Through the expansion of awareness in the glorious line of heroes, a pure mind directed toward the guru becomes the cause for either liberation or attainment.
sanskrit_cite: tacca saṃvidvikāsena śrīmadvīrāvalīpade guravastu vimuktau vā siddhau vā vimalā matiḥ

plain_english: In both liberation and attainment, whatever is pleasing to the mind and fit for worship can be the cause, because its effectiveness comes from the completeness of conditions operating through necessity.
sanskrit_cite: heturityubhayatrāpi yāgauko yanmanoramam niyatiprāṇatāyogātsāmagrītastu yadyapi

plain_english: Although attainments and purity of being may both arise, a person whose heart has become pure reflects on whatever is best of all in that situation.
sanskrit_cite: siddhayo bhāvavaimalyaṃ tathāpi nikhilottamam vimalībhūtahṛdayo yattatra pratibimbayet

plain_english: What one seeks becomes fruitful through firmness, and the Sāraśāstra says that the one who is free of conceptual construction truly succeeds.
sanskrit_cite: sādhyaṃ tadasya dārḍhyena saphalatvāya kalpate uktaṃ śrīsāraśāstre ca nirvikalpo hi sidhyati

plain_english: Those who remain caught in conceptual construction struggle even when they perform what the ritual prescribes, but when that underlying power is truly accessed, the mantras rise clearly and effectively.
sanskrit_cite: kliśyante savikalpāstu kalpokte@pi kṛte sati tadākramya balaṃ mantrā ayamevodayaḥ sphuṭaḥ

plain_english: Statements from the Spanda and others make this same point clear: in worship, recitation, and absorption, the same principle holds whether one seeks attainment or liberation.
sanskrit_cite: ityādibhiḥ spandavākyairetadeva nirūpitam tasmātsiddhyai vimuktyai vā pūjājapasamādhiṣu

plain_english: Wherever the heart comes to rest in a beautiful stillness, that place is fit for worship; having reached it, a purified practitioner may remain outwardly engaged while grounded there.
sanskrit_cite: tatsthānaṃ yatra viśrāntisundaraṃ hṛdayaṃ bhavet yāgaukaḥ prāpya śuddhātmā bahireva vyavasthitaḥ

plain_english: For the establishment of outer worship, one should perform a general nyāsa using the Mātṛkā, the Mālinī, or both, either in sequence or in non-sequence.
sanskrit_cite: nyāsaṃ sāmānyataḥ kuryādbahiryāgaprasiddhaye mātṛkāṃ mālinīṃ vātha dvitayaṃ vā kramākramāt

plain_english: Using the two modes of emission and withdrawal, one should place the elements one by one and in pairs on the forehead, face, eyes, ears, nose, cheeks, teeth, and lips.
sanskrit_cite: sṛṣṭyapyayadvayaiḥ kuryādekaikaṃ saṃghaśo dviśaḥ lalāṭavaktre dṛkkarṇanāsāgaṇḍaradauṣṭhage

plain_english: In this stage, sixteen phonemes ending with visarga are placed in pairs, including on the crown-tuft and tongue, while the ka and ca groups are assigned to the right and left shoulders, arms, hands, fingers, and nails.
sanskrit_cite: dvaye dvaye śikhājihve visargāntāstu ṣoḍaśa dakṣānyayoḥ skandhabāhukarāṅgulinakhe kacau

plain_english: One should place the ṭa and ta groups in order on the hips, thighs, and so forth, and place the pa group on the sides, back, belly, and heart, making a ninefold assignment.
sanskrit_cite: vargau ṭatau kramātkaṭyāmūrvādiṣu niyojayet pavargaṃ pārśvayoḥ pṛṣṭhe jaṭhare hṛdyatho nava

plain_english: This completes the Mātṛkā nyāsa, extending through the bodily constituents from skin to seed, and now the Mālinī nyāsa is explained.
sanskrit_cite: tvagraktamāṃsasūtrāsthivasāśukrapurogamān ityeṣa mātṛkānyāso mālinyāstu nirūpyate

plain_english: Place na, ṛ, ṝ, ḷ, and ḹ on the crest and the garland of the head, and tha on the crown. Assign the eyes above and below, place ī on the nose, ṇu and ṇū on the two seals, and place the corresponding letters on the two ears.
sanskrit_cite: na śikhā ṛ ṝ ḷ ḷḷ ca śiromālā tha mastakam netrāṇi cordhve dho@nye ī ghrāṇaṃ mudre ṇu ṇū śrutī

plain_english: Place the ba-ka group with i and ā in order on the mouth, teeth, tongue, and palate. Place va, bha, and ya on the throat and the right and left shoulders, and place ḍa and ḍha on the two arms.
sanskrit_cite: bakavarga+i+ā vaktradantajihvāgiri kramāt vabhayāḥ kaṇṭhadakṣādiskandhayorbhujayorḍaḍhau

plain_english: Place ṭha on the two hands, jha and ña on the branches, and jra and ṭa on the trident and skull. Place pa on the heart and cha and la on the two breasts. Mā, associated with milk, and sa joined with visarga are said to be the life-breath.
sanskrit_cite: ṭho hastayorjhañau śākhā jraṭau śūlakapālake pa hṛcchalau stanau kṣīramā sa jīvo visargayuk

plain_english: Ha is declared to be the vital breath. Ṣa and kṣa go to the belly and the navel. The group ending with ma goes to the hips, the private parts, and the pair of thighs, and likewise to the two knees.
sanskrit_cite: prāṇo havarṇaḥ kathitaḥ ṣakṣāvudaranābhigau maśāntā kaṭiguhyoruyugmagā jānunī tathā

plain_english: Place e and ai, and the pair that follows them, on the two shins, and place da and pha on the two feet. This is the goddess Mālinī, because she is stirred into activity by the possessor of power.
sanskrit_cite: eaikārau tatparau tu jaṅghe caraṇagau daphau ityeṣā mālinī devī śaktimatkṣobhitā yataḥ

plain_english: Because it enters into ritual efficacy, that body is, in ultimate truth, a body of Śakti. It arises from the mutual stirring of the seeds and wombs, through an emissive arising.
sanskrit_cite: kṛtyāveśāttataḥ śāktī tanuḥ sā paramārthataḥ anyonyaṃ bījayonīnāṃ kṣobhādvaisargikodayāt

plain_english: What accomplishment would she not grant, or what deficiency would she not fill? Although the intermixture of wombs, seeds, and phonemes exists in many forms, her power is complete.
sanskrit_cite: kāṃ kāṃ siddhiṃ na vitaretkiṃ vā nyūnaṃ na pūrayet yonibījārṇasāṃkaryaṃ bahudhā yadyapi sthitam

plain_english: Even so, the sequence beginning with na and ending with pha is proclaimed as the primary one. By uttering from pha to na, the whole circle of the path is formed.
sanskrit_cite: tathāpi nādiphānto@yaṃ kramo mukhyaḥ prakīrtitaḥ phakārādisamuccārānnakārānte@dhvamaṇḍalam

plain_english: When withdrawn into consciousness, she is full and complete, so how could she truly be described by words? For that reason the scriptures speak of her in many ways, through forms such as kula, puttalika, and others.
sanskrit_cite: saṃhṛtya saṃvidyā pūrṇā sā śabdairvarṇyate katham ataḥ śāstreṣu bahudhā kulaputtalikādibhiḥ

plain_english: Although she is sung in many divisions, this Malini, beginning with na and ending with pha, is the primary one. She is the inner, uncontracted form of Bhairava, who is the mass of sound.
sanskrit_cite: bhedairgītā hi mukhyeyaṃ nādiphānteti mālinī śabdarāśerbhairavasya yānucchūnatayāntarī

plain_english: She is like a mother because she brings forth what is to come, and so she is called the mother. As Malini, garlanded and upheld by the Rudras, she supports both accomplishment and liberation.
sanskrit_cite: sā māteva bhaviṣyattvāttenāsau mātṛkoditā mālinī mālitā rudrairdhārikā siddhimokṣayoḥ

plain_english: She flowers in fruits and is worthy of worship, like a six-footed bee in the sound of withdrawal. Because of ra and la, she is endowed with powers of withdrawal, giving, taking, and more.
sanskrit_cite: phaleṣu puṣpitā pūjyā saṃhāradhvaniṣaṭpadī saṃhāradānādānādiśaktiyuktā yato ralau

plain_english: Śambhunātha declared that this sound-array Mālinī is of the nature of Śiva and Śakti, remembered as one.
sanskrit_cite: ekatvena smarantīti śaṃbhunātho nirūcivān śabdarāśirmālinī ca śivaśaktyātmakaṃ tvidam

plain_english: Because each is full by Śiva-Śakti nature, this restores what is lost in rite, power, or form.
sanskrit_cite: ekaikatrāpi pūrṇatvācchivaśaktisvabhāvatā tena bhraṣṭe vidhau vīrye svarūpe vānayā param

plain_english: Mantras that are placed are filled by replacement and give that fruit, as said in Śrīpūrvatantra, even without special rite.
sanskrit_cite: mantrā nyastāḥ punarnyāsātpūryante tatphalapradāḥ uktaṃ śrīpūrvatantre ca viśeṣavidhihīnite

plain_english: For the purpose of the desire-active body, Mālinī is placed; this qualifier is determined as cause and cause-meaning, though the source differs.
sanskrit_cite: nyasyecchāktaśarīrārthaṃ bhinnayoni tu mālinīm viśeṣaṇamidaṃ hetau hetvarthaśca nirūpitaḥ

plain_english: This was spoken here for accomplishing the desired fruit: even mantras with collyrium, Garuḍa and others, are not supreme.
sanskrit_cite: yatheṣṭaphalasiddhyai cetyatraivedamabhāṣata sāñjanā api ye mantrā gāruḍādyā na te param

plain_english: Filled by Mālinī, they accomplish by strength; but for liberation, even one desiring fruit places another mantra here as Mālinī.
sanskrit_cite: mālinyā pūritāḥ sidhdyai balādeva tu muktaye tasmātphalepsurapyanya mantraṃ nyasyātra mālinīm

plain_english: Place after reciting, and recite without effort for release; thus place Mātṛkā or Mālinī in order, both.
sanskrit_cite: nyasyejjaptvāpica japedayatnādapavṛktaye ityevaṃ mātṛkāṃ nyasyenmālinīṃ vā kramāddvayam

plain_english: According to accomplishment or liberation, letters are placed; both simultaneously use akṣa-hrīṃ and napha-hrīṃ, masses of union and separation.
sanskrit_cite: siddhimuktyanusārādvā varṇānvā yugapaddvayoḥ akṣahrīṃ naphahrīmetau piṇḍau saṃghāvihānayoḥ

plain_english: The expressive ones are placement; when placement is done by these two, it is single or with limb-body-Brahma, or its reverse.
sanskrit_cite: vācakau nyāsa etābhyāṃ kṛte nyāse@thavaikakaḥ eṣa cāṅgatanubrahmayukto vā tadviparyayaḥ

plain_english: In collective placement, the two masses are separate; they are placed in order or without order, then place only one and join.
sanskrit_cite: sāmudāyikavinyāse pṛthak piṇḍāvimau kramāt akramādathavā nyasyedekamevātha yojayet

plain_english: One desiring accomplishment by rite should perform more rite; even one not desiring receives that rite for more of his own fruit.
sanskrit_cite: kriyayā siddhikāmo yaḥ sa kriyāṃ bhūyasīṃ caret anīpsurapi yastasmai bhūyase svaphalāya sā

plain_english: One desiring accomplishment by meditation and recitation should do rite for purification by his own will, then more according to prior rule.
sanskrit_cite: yastu dhyānajapābhyāsaiḥ siddhīpsuḥ sa kriyāṃ param saṃskṛtyai svecchayā kuryāt prāṅnayenātha bhūyasīm

plain_english: The aspirant for liberation should perform for him as desired; the attainment of Shiva-nature is indeed the purpose of these nyasa and related rites.
sanskrit_cite: mumukṣuratha tasmai vā yathābhīṣṭaṃ samācaret śivatāpattirevārtho hyeṣāṃ nyāsādikarmaṇām

plain_english: Having thus performed nyasa in the argha vessel, one should perform the rite according to the stated rule; thereafter worship with the installed mantras.
sanskrit_cite: evaṃ nyāsaṃ vidhāyārghapātre vidhimupācaret uktanītyaiva tatpaścāt pūjayennyastavācakaiḥ

plain_english: Because all beings attain perfection from Shiva, and from the full one comes non-difference of agents in this worship.
sanskrit_cite: yataḥ samastabhāvānāṃ śivātsiddhimayādatho pūrṇādavyatirekitvaṃ kārakāṇāmihārcayā

plain_english: The whole host of agents is shown as non-different from Shiva; in the example of worship one attains all, even going and the rest.
sanskrit_cite: samastaṃ kārakavrātaṃ śivābhinnaṃ pradarśitam pūjodāharaṇe sarvaṃ vyaśnute gamanādyapi

plain_english: As a horse that has come under the rider's control through the bridle's freedom, though mounted in battle, does not transgress that training.
sanskrit_cite: yathāhi vāhakaṭakabhramasvātantryamāgataḥ aśvaḥ saṃgrāmarūḍho@pi tāṃ śikṣāṃ nātivartate

plain_english: So the agent habituated by worship-practice and made Shiva-like, though going or standing, abandons duality of agents.
sanskrit_cite: tathārcanakriyābhyāsaśivībhāvitakārakaḥ gacchaṃstiṣṭhannapi dvaitaṃ kārakāṇāṃ vyapojjhati

plain_english: Thus for one established in unity-practice, this universe suddenly, by force, like a dancer, may flash as full Shiva-nature.
sanskrit_cite: tathaikyābhyāsaniṣṭhasyākramādviśvamidaṃ haṭhāt saṃpūrṇaśivatākṣobhanarīnartadiva sphuret

plain_english: Our supreme guru said in the praise of worship: 'Ah, what sweet taste, what festival of Shiva-worship!'
sanskrit_cite: uvāca pūjanastotre hyasmākaṃ paramo guruḥ aho svādurasaḥ ko@pi śivapūjāmayotsavaḥ

plain_english: The agitation of thirty-six principles, where it shines, is for full Shiva-entry into the universe; those who worship.
sanskrit_cite: ṣaṭtriṃśato@pi tattvānāṃ kṣobho yatrollasatyalam tadetādṛkpūrṇaśivaviśvāveśāya ye@rcanam

plain_english: They are Shiva indeed; what fruit for the full ones? Even without knowledge and yoga, action like nyasa and worship.
sanskrit_cite: kurvanti te śivā eva tānpūrṇānprati kiṃ phalam vināpi jñānayogābhyāṃ kriyā nyāsārcanādikā

plain_english: Thus by granting unity-samapatti, bestowing other fruit, the practitioner too has attained mantra-unity with that good vipra.
sanskrit_cite: itthamaikyasamāpattidānātparaphalapradā sādhakasyāpi tatsadvipradamantraikatāṃ gatam

plain_english: The universe would quickly attain unobstructedness and its own perfection; it is said by the Supreme Lord: neither rule nor worship procedure.
sanskrit_cite: viśvaṃ vrajadavighnatvaṃ svāṃ siddhiṃ śīghramāvahet uktaṃ ca parameśena na vidhirnārcanakramaḥ

plain_english: Only through remembrance is success desired; thus ritual action gives absorption in that, because of this.
sanskrit_cite: kevalaṃ smaraṇātsiddhirvāñchiteti matādiṣu tadevaṃ tanmayībhāvadāyinyarcākriyā yataḥ

plain_english: Through unity of all agents, her supreme body becomes identity with the support of the sacrificer by the order of place-purification rite.
sanskrit_cite: samastakārakaikātmyaṃ tenāsyāḥ paramaṃ vapuḥ yaṣṭrādhārasya tādātmyaṃ sthānaśuddhividhikramāt

plain_english: By nyāsa order, the sacrificer, offering, support, instruments, gifts, and transmissions attain identity with Śiva-ness.
sanskrit_cite: yaṣṭṛyājyatadādhārakaraṇādānasaṃpradāḥ nyāsakrameṇa śivatātādātmyamadhiśerate

plain_english: The argha vessel is the recipient, therefore it is taken; whatever water and instruments are situated in it serve purification or worship.
sanskrit_cite: arghapātramapādānaṃ tasmādādīyate yataḥ yacca tatsthaṃ jalādyetatkaraṇaṃ śodhane@rcane

plain_english: All touched by drops from the argha vessel becomes pure; other purity will arise from contact with Śiva-sun rays.
sanskrit_cite: arghapātrāmbuvipruḍbhiḥ spṛṣṭaṃ sarvaṃ hi śudhyati śivārkakarasaṃsparśātkānyā śuddhirbhaviṣyati

plain_english: The Lord said in the holy former scripture: in that argha-vessel rite, one should not provide any unpurified thing at all.
sanskrit_cite: ūce śrīpūrvaśāstre tadarghapātravidhau vibhuḥ na cāsaṃśodhitaṃ vastu kiṃcidapyupakalpayet

plain_english: Therefore all is pure, even what is impure; that is pure, and impurity is to be known from the intention of binding the paśu.
sanskrit_cite: tena śuddhaṃ tu sarvaṃ yadaśuddhamapi tacchuci aśuddhatā ca vijñeyā paśutacchāsanāśayāt

plain_english: From one's own state or from what was previously provided, therefore whatever is present here is by the grace of consciousness.
sanskrit_cite: svatādavasthyātpūrvasmādathavāpyupakalpitāt tena yadyadihāsannaṃ saṃvidaścidanugrahāt

plain_english: However much that is extremely suitable in this sacrifice, like a living being, by this method of reasoning when existence is far from knowledge.
sanskrit_cite: kiyato@pi tadatyantaṃ yogyaṃ yāge@tra jīvavat anena nayayogena yadāsattividūrate

plain_english: When consciousness arises, then there one should declare suitability or unsuitability; for heroes indeed here, mutually, the nectar of one's own image.
sanskrit_cite: saṃvideti tadā tatra yogyāyogyatvamādiśet vīrāṇāmata eveha mithaḥ svapratimāmṛtam

plain_english: Entered into each sacrifice rite, self-realized gurus raise up consciousness that is submerged; but that is well.
sanskrit_cite: tattadyāgavidhāviṣṭaṃ gurubhirbhāvitātmabhiḥ unmajjayati nirmagnāṃ saṃvidaṃ yattu suṣṭhu tat

plain_english: For worship, suitable bliss arises because consciousness rises up; therefore it submerges the predominance of non-conscious body and the like.
sanskrit_cite: arcāyai yogyamānando yasmādunmagnatā citaḥ tenācidrūpadehādiprādhānyavinimajjakam

plain_english: Whatever produces bliss, is fit for worship, and captivates the heart is therefore praised in the teachings of Kula, Krama, the transcendent Trika essence, and others.
sanskrit_cite: ānandajananaṃ pūjāyogyaṃ hṛdayahāri yat ataḥ kulakramottīrṇatrikasāramatādiṣu

plain_english: Wine, kādambarī, śīdhu, and such substances have supreme greatness, yet in the teaching meant for bound souls they are restricted in order to maintain worldly order.
sanskrit_cite: madyakādambarīśīdhudravyādermahimā param lokasthitiṃ racayituṃ madyādeḥ paśuśāsane

plain_english: In that teaching it is declared impure, yet in some contexts there is purity; for example, the five cow products are purifying, as are soma remains and ritual vessels.
sanskrit_cite: proktā hyaśuddhistatraiva tasya kvāpi viśuddhatā pañcagavye pavitratvaṃ somacarṇanapātrayoḥ

plain_english: There are rules such as the concluding bath, holding the black antelope horn in the hand, not performing the sacrifice without the wife, and treating all deities as equal.
sanskrit_cite: vidhiścāvabhṛthasnānaṃ haste kṛṣṇaviṣāṇitā na patnyā ca vinā yāgaḥ sarvadaivatatulyatā

plain_english: Even in the scriptures meant for bound souls, the great lord showed a liquor offering in a brahma session and an offering of omentum, intestine, and heart.
sanskrit_cite: surāhutirbrahmasatre vapāntrahṛdayāhutiḥ pāśaveṣvapi śāstreṣu tadadarśi maheśinā

plain_english: In opposed judgments, one says the goose is to be eaten and another says it is not; amid such confusion, clarity is like a lamp shining at midnight in terrible snowy darkness.
sanskrit_cite: ghorāndhyahaimananiśāmadhyagāciradīptivat bhakṣyo haṃso na bhakṣyo@sāviti ripratipattiṣu

plain_english: Among smārta teachings, the one principle that prevails is purification through non-difference from Śiva; for ignorance, mere appeal to the Veda, attachment, aversion, and such defects undermine authority.
sanskrit_cite: smārtīṣu vijayatyeko yaḥ śivābhedaśuddhikaḥ ajñatvavedādarśitvarāgadveṣādayo hyamī

plain_english: These defects can uproot the authority of the sages' own words; even in the Veda, what is said not to be eaten is taught elsewhere as something to be eaten.
sanskrit_cite: munīnāṃ vacasi svasminprāmāṇyonmūlanakṣamāḥ vede@pi yadabhakṣyaṃ tadbhakṣyamityupadiśyate

plain_english: Injunction and prohibition do not rest on one single basis; if in a particular context something is not to be eaten, then that is how it stands there, and the matter is resolved accordingly.
sanskrit_cite: na vidhipratiṣedhākhyadharmayorekamāspadam atha tatra na tadbhakṣyaṃ tadā tena tathā tataḥ

plain_english: Thus, because their domains differ, Vedic revelation does not override the word of Śiva; only if their domains were the same would there be a relation of overruling and being overruled.
sanskrit_cite: evaṃ viṣayabhedānno śivokterbādhikā śrutiḥ kvacidviṣayatulyatvādbādhyabādhakatā yadi

plain_english: If their domains were equal, Vedic revelation itself would be overruled; this has already been established. Now we return to the present topic: after performing installation on the body and the offering vessel.
sanskrit_cite: tadbādhyā śrutireveti prāgevaitannirūpitam prakṛtaṃ brūmahe kṛtvā nyāsaṃ dehārghapātrayoḥ

plain_english: After sprinkling all the worship implements with drops of water from the common offering vessel, one should then perform the external worship.
sanskrit_cite: sāmānyamarghapātrāmbhovipruḍbhiḥ prokṣya cākhilam yāgopakaraṇaṃ paścādbāhyayāgaṃ samācaret

plain_english: In a circle of light, in space, or on a well-smeared ground, one should worship the mothers, who stand on the trident, the sun, the bull, and Nandin, and also worship the lord of the field.
sanskrit_cite: prabhāmaṇḍalake khe vā suliptāyāṃ ca vā bhuvi triśūlārkavṛṣāndikasthā mātaraḥ kṣetrapaṃ yajet

plain_english: One should also worship the yoginīs, either with separate mantras joined with oṃ, namas, and their names, or with a single utterance, as they are called the outer retinue.
sanskrit_cite: yoginīśca pṛthaṅmantrairoṃnamonāmayojitaiḥ ekoccāreṇa vā bāhyaparivāretiśabditāḥ

plain_english: In worship the mantra is oṃ, the name in the fourth-case form, and namas. Having thus worshipped outside, one should sprinkle the doorway and then worship it.
sanskrit_cite: tāro nāma caturthyantaṃ namaścetyarcane manuḥ evaṃ bahiḥ pūjayitvā dvāraṃ prokṣya prapūjayet

plain_english: This procedure is seen in the teaching of the Three-headed One and others. Above the doorway one should worship Gaṇeśa and Lakṣmī, on the right and left, and then continue with those associated with them.
sanskrit_cite: triśiraḥśāsanādau ca sa dṛṣṭo vidhirucyate gaṇeśalakṣmyau dvārordhve dakṣe vāme tayoḥ punaḥ

plain_english: In the middle one should place Vāgīśvarī, and likewise the pair Diṇḍi and Mahodara, in order on their own right and left, following that same sequence.
sanskrit_cite: madhye vāgīśvarīṃ diṇḍimahodarayugaṃ tathā kramātsvadakṣavāmasthaṃ tathaitena krameṇa ca

plain_english: One should properly worship each one: Nandi and Kāla, the river who flows by three paths, Kālindī, and the goat-faced and ram-faced pair, on the door branches beginning from one's own right.
sanskrit_cite: ekaikaṃ pūjayetsamyaṅ nandikālau trimārgagām kālindīṃ chāgameṣāsyau svadakṣāddvāḥsthaśākhayoḥ

plain_english: Below the threshold one should worship Dehalī, Ananta, Īśa, and the supporting power; in the middle of the doorway one should worship the great weapon together with Sarasvatī.
sanskrit_cite: adhodehalyananteśādhāraśaktīśca pūjayet dvāramadhye sarasvatyā mahāstraṃ pūjayedamī

plain_english: All these, situated on the lotus support, are declared to be destroyers of obstacles. In their worship the mantra is used as before, with an arrangement of two lamps.
sanskrit_cite: padmādhāragatāḥ sarve@pyuditā vighnanāśakāḥ pūjane pūrvavanmantro dīpakadvayakalpitaḥ

plain_english: One should perform the worship here with offering water, flowers, touch, incense, food offerings, and homage; and the offering water should be prepared with excellent substances.
sanskrit_cite: arghapuṣpasamālambhadhūpanaivedyavandanaiḥ pūjāṃ kuryādihārghaścāpyuttamadravyayojitaḥ

plain_english: Or one may perform the worship of the doorway deities with a single utterance. If one performs secret worship, then that outer retinue is included in that condensed form.
sanskrit_cite: ekoccāreṇa vā kuryāddvāḥsthadaivatapūjanam rahasyapūjāṃ cetkuryāttadbāhyaparivārakam

plain_english: One may worship the doorway deities inwardly before the deity according to the visualized sequence. Then, throwing a flower consecrated by the weapon mantra into the blazing shrine, one destroys obstacles.
sanskrit_cite: dvāḥsthāṃśca pūjayedantardevāgre kalpanākramāt kṣiptvāstrajaptaṃ kusumaṃ jvaladveśmani vghnanut

plain_english: Having entered, one should look upon the shrine with a gaze empowered by Śiva's rays; then one should bind the directions with the weapon mantra and cover them all with the armor mantra.
sanskrit_cite: praviśya śivaraśmīddhadṛśā veśmāvalokayet diśo@streṇa ca badhnīyācchādayedvarmaṇākhilāḥ

plain_english: There the seeker for liberation should enter facing the northern direction, for the fire of Aghora burns away the bonds that bind.
sanskrit_cite: tatrottarāśābhimukho mumukṣustādṛśāya vā viśettathā hyaghorāgniḥ pāśānpluṣyati bandhakān

plain_english: Even though we speak of directions like east and west, there is no such thing as direction by itself, for no single direction can be cognized without a limiting condition.
sanskrit_cite: yadyapyasti na diṅnāma kācitpūrvāparādikā pratyayo hi na tasyāḥ syādekasyā anupāhiteḥ

plain_english: If someone says that direction is just a limiting condition called east and so on, then how could such a mere condition account for real variety?
sanskrit_cite: upādhiḥ pūrvatādiṣṭa iti cettatkṛtaṃ diśā upādhimātraṃ tu tathā vaicitryāya kathaṃ bhavet

plain_english: Therefore it is this light of consciousness, appearing in the form of objects, that boldly displays the variety known as the division into east and other directions.
sanskrit_cite: tasmātsaṃvitprakāśo@yaṃ mūrtyābhāsanabhāgataḥ pūrvādidigvibhāgākhyavaicitryollekhadurmadaḥ

plain_english: Whatever is always fit to be taken up by light is above, being of the nature of light, while what is unfit for contact is below.
sanskrit_cite: tatra yadyatprakāśena sadā svīkaraṇe kṣamam tadevordhvaṃ prakāśātma sparśāyogyamadhaḥ punaḥ

plain_english: What is only slightly luminous is the middle, and from that the directions arise; when light spreads toward what can be slightly illuminated, that is the front.
sanskrit_cite: kiṃcitprakāśatā madhyaṃ tato vai diksamudbhavaḥ kiṃcitprakāśayogyasya saṃmukhaṃ prasaratpuraḥ

plain_english: What is turned away is behind, so front and back arise as a pair; when light faces an object and grasps it, its rays become more abundant.
sanskrit_cite: parāṅmukhaṃ tu tatpaścāditi digdvayamāgatam prakāśaḥ saṃmukhaṃ vastu gṛhītvodriktaraśmikaḥ

plain_english: Where light stands in conformity, that is called the right; and what stands in front of that right side is taught to be the left.
sanskrit_cite: yatra tiṣṭhoddakṣiṇaṃ tatprakāśasyānukūlyataḥ dakṣiṇasya puraḥsaṃsthaṃ vāmamityupadiśyate

plain_english: That same illuminated field, gentle like the touch of moonlight, gives rise in this way to the first set of four directions through resting in the middle.
sanskrit_cite: tatprakāśitameyendusparśasaumyaṃ tadeva hi evamāśācatuṣke@sminmadhyaviśrāntiyogataḥ

plain_english: With another set of four, the directions become eight, each presided over by its own power; all this arises within the supreme, boon-granting light of Śiva.
sanskrit_cite: catuṣkamanyattenāṣṭau diśastattadadhiṣṭhitāḥ evaṃ prakāśamātre@sminvarade parame śive

plain_english: The division of directions is established both in the world and in scripture, for Sadāśiva is taught in sequence as having a body made of five mantras.
sanskrit_cite: digvibhāgaḥ sthito loke śāstre@pica tathocyate kramātsadāśivādhīśaḥ pañcamantratanuryataḥ

plain_english: By the division into Īśāna, Aghora, Vāma, Sadyojāta, and the lower face, the directions are mapped out: Īśāna is above because of its luminosity, and the extending eastern face corresponds to that light.
sanskrit_cite: īśanraghoravāmākhyasadyo@dhobhedato diśaḥ īśa ūrdhvaṃ prakāśatvātpūrvaṃ vaktraṃ prasāri yat

plain_english: Puruṣa is identified in this scheme, the fierce Aghora is the south, the gentle Vāma is the left, and Sadyojāta, being turned away, is designated as the west.
sanskrit_cite: puruṣo dakṣiṇācaṇḍo vāmā vāmastu saumyakaḥ parāṅmukhatayā sadyaḥ paścimā paribhāṣyate

plain_english: The nether face is below because of its lack of luminosity, and indeed space, wind, fire, water, and earth are the faces of that Lord.
sanskrit_cite: pātālavaktramadharamaprakāśatayā sthiteḥ khamarudvahnijalabhūkhāni vaktrāṇyamuṣya hi

plain_english: As the primary element, space alone is said to be above and made of light, while below that same principle is clearly non-luminous.
sanskrit_cite: mukhyatvena khamevordhvaṃ prakāśamayamucyate tadeva mukhyato@dhastādaprakāśaṃ yataḥ sphuṭam

plain_english: In the middle, what is luminous is neither merely something to be illuminated nor simply its opposite; because it is seen through luminosity, a set of four directions arises there.
sanskrit_cite: madhye tu yatprakāśaṃ tanna prakāśyaṃ na cetarat prakāśatvāddiśyamānamato@smindikcatuṣṭayam

plain_english: Thus the Lord whose body is the five mantras is the sovereign of all directions, and after him Īśa, Rudra, Viṣṇu, and Brahmā are likewise established.
sanskrit_cite: pañcamantratanurnātha itthaṃ viśvadigīśvaraḥ tato@pīśastathā rudro viṣṇurbrahmā tathā sthitaḥ

plain_english: Viṣṇu and Brahmā do not have a fifth face, because they are powers of differentiation concerned with maintenance and creation, not with that higher upward manifestation.
sanskrit_cite: ūrdhvābhivyaktyayogyatvādviṣṇordhātuśca pañcamam na vaktraṃ tau bhedamayau sṛṣṭisthitiprabhū yataḥ

plain_english: Their division of directions comes from four faces; if a fifth were joined to them, those two would abandon their own nature.
sanskrit_cite: digvibhāgastu tajjo@sti vadanānāṃ catuṣṭayāt pañcamasya yujitve tau parityaktanijātmakau

plain_english: Therefore, even within the cosmic egg, the Lord's power of knowledge, appearing as the sun dense with light, makes the division of the directions.
sanskrit_cite: tato brahmāṇḍamadhye@pi jñānaśaktirvibho raviḥ diśāṃ vibhāgaṃ kurute prakāśaghanavṛttimān

plain_english: For example, at the equinox, where the sun is first seen is called east, and where its shadow falls is called west.
sanskrit_cite: tathāhi viṣuvadyoge yataḥ pūrvaṃ pradṛśyate tatpūrva yatra tacchāyā tatpaścimamudāhṛtam

plain_english: As the sun moves on its course, what lies to its left is the south, where it shines with fierce rays as if blazing intensely.
sanskrit_cite: tasmiñjigamiṣorasya yatsavyaṃ tattu dakṣiṇam tatraiṣa caṇḍatejobhirbhāti jājvalyamānavat

plain_english: What lies in front of that is the left, slightly touched by its light; therefore it is gentle, yet not without light.
sanskrit_cite: tatpurovarti vāmaṃ tu tadbhāsā khacitaṃ manāk tata eva hi somyaṃ tannacāpi hyaprakāśakam

plain_english: Where the sun sets is established as the west; and even there, for some, the earlier light can still be seen.
sanskrit_cite: yatrāsāvastamabhyeti tatpaścimamiti sthitiḥ tatraiva paścime yeṣāṃ prākprakāśāvalokanam

plain_english: That same order was determined before for these as in sound; that direction is so, and its fruit-giving remains even in reversal.
sanskrit_cite: tadeva pūrvameteṣāṃ yathādhvani nirūpitam sā sā dikca tathā tasya phaladāpi viparyaye

plain_english: Varied fruit-attainment depends on light; thus direction may be sun-dependent, various, and such.
sanskrit_cite: vicitre phalasaṃpattiḥ prakāśādhīnikā yataḥ itthaṃ sūryāśrayā diksyātsā vicitrāpi tādṛśī

plain_english: Presided over by the great lord bearing varied form; what more need be said of the worshipper facing that?
sanskrit_cite: adhiṣṭhitā maheśena citratadrūpadhāriṇā kiṃ vātibahunā yo@sau yaṣṭā tatsaṃmukhāditaḥ

plain_english: Directions are divided east, south, north, west; that direction-division made according to own course is always Shiva.
sanskrit_cite: diśo@pi pravibhajyante prāksavyottarapaścimāḥ svānusārakṛtaṃ taṃ ca digvibhāgaṃ sadā śivaḥ

plain_english: He presides like the sun from varied body; even self-risen directions have own lords, and Indra and others indeed preside.
sanskrit_cite: adhitiṣṭhatyarkamiva sa vicitravapuryataḥ svotthā api diśaḥ sveśāḥ śakrādyā hyadhiśerate

plain_english: They are indeed portions of light-power, following light; whatever lordship of light is Indra, but that greatness is something else.
sanskrit_cite: te hi prakāśaśaktyaṃśāḥ prakāśānuvidhāyinaḥ prakāśasya yadaiśvaryaṃ sa indro yattu tanmahaḥ

plain_english: He is fire in the controller-desired state; Yama, Raksha, then those; Varuna and that; from unsteadiness air is called.
sanskrit_cite: so@gniryantṛtvabhīmatve yamo rakṣastadūnimā prakāśyaṃ varuṇastacca cāñcalyādvāyurucyate

plain_english: By accumulation of being, the wealth-lord at its decay is all-pervading; unseen form, endless; above Brahma, expander, all-pervading.
sanskrit_cite: bhāvasañcayayogena vitteśastatkṣaye vibhuḥ adṛṣṭavigraho@nanto brahmordhve vṛṃhako vibhuḥ

plain_english: Power-portions of light only; world-guardians are declared by that. Thus even self-dependent form; direction-sun is taught.
sanskrit_cite: prakāśasyaiva śaktyaṃśā lokapāstena kīrtitāḥ itthaṃ svādhīnarūpāpi diksaurī tūpadiśyate

plain_english: There all indeed attains unwavering light-nature, as all-pervading wind is fanned by a fan.
sanskrit_cite: tatra sarvo hi niṣkampaṃ prakāśatvaṃ prapadyate sarvago@pyanilo yadvadvyajanenopavījitaḥ

plain_english: The awakened would do his own action, duty-removal and so on; like that, all-pervading, all Indra-powers clearly.
sanskrit_cite: prabuddhaḥ svāṃ kriyāṃ kuryāddharmanirṇodanādikām tadvatsarvagatāḥ sarvā aindyādyāḥ śaktayaḥ sphuṭam

plain_english: Adepts awakened by breath give various desired fruit; thus sun-power with direction-lords, Brahma, Vishnu, Isha, Sau, Shiva.
sanskrit_cite: sādhakāśvāsasaṃbuddhāstattatsveṣṭaphalapradāḥ evaṃ saurī digīśānabrahmaviṣṇvīśasauśivaiḥ

plain_english: Presided over by firm reassurance, giving various fruit; the adept may worship field, mandala, or house.
sanskrit_cite: adhiṣṭhitā samāśvāsadārḍhyāttattatphalapradā sādhako yacca vā kṣetraṃ maṇḍalaṃ veśma vā bhajet

plain_english: Standing according to that, Shankara becomes middle; he indeed is all-presider by middleness, its who.
sanskrit_cite: sthitastadanusāreṇa madhyībhavati śaṃkaraḥ sa hi sarvamadhiṣṭhātā mādhyasthyeneti tasya yaḥ

plain_english: Sun-related light before thus may be direction-establishment; of the lord standing in the middle, to grasp southern greatness.
sanskrit_cite: sauraḥ prakāśastatpūrvamitthaṃ syāddigvyavasthitiḥ tanmadhyasthitanāthasya grahītuṃ dakṣiṇaṃ mahaḥ

plain_english: North-facing may be to grasp western; east-facing, having sat in own place, should perform body-purification.
sanskrit_cite: udaṅmukhaḥ syāt pāścātyaṃ grahītuṃ pūrvatomukhaḥ upaviśya nijasthāne dehaśuddhiṃ samācaret

plain_english: Weapon risen as flame from thumb tip; having meditated, by its flames burn the body outside and inside.
sanskrit_cite: aṅguṣṭhāgrātkālavahnijvālābhāsvaramutthitam astraṃ dhyātvā tacchikhābhirbahirantardahettanum

plain_english: Burning and destruction are thus called; destroyer named mantra; radiance thus named own thought-essence.
sanskrit_cite: dāhaśca dhvaṃsa evokto dhvaṃsakaṃ mantrasaṃjñitam tejastathābhilāpākhyasvavikalparasombhitam

plain_english: By that mantra-fire burning in body and eightfold city, so from destruction of body-city-ego arises.
sanskrit_cite: tena mantrāgninā dāho dehe puryaṣṭake tathā dehapuryaṣṭakāhantāvidhvaṃsādeva jāyate

plain_english: Not indeed by mere existence is the body like another body; in egoity indeed is bodiness; that destroyed, that burns certainly.
sanskrit_cite: nahi sadbhāvamātreṇa deho@sāvanyadehavat ahantāyāṃ hi dehatvaṃ sā dhvastā taddaheddhruvam

plain_english: Burden of body-purification as ash then who standing; shaking him with armor-wind, should stand in pure consciousness-self.
sanskrit_cite: taddehasaṃskārabharo bhasmatvenātha yaḥ sthitaḥ taṃ varmavāyunādhūya tiṣṭhecchuddhacidātmani

plain_english: In that steady waveless, having attained absorption, of consciousness, from creative nature first attains waviness.
sanskrit_cite: tasmindhruve nistaraṅge samāpattimupāgataḥ saṃvidaḥ sṛṣṭidharmitvādādyāmeti taraṅgitām

plain_english: That itself form thus called, syllable-bindu-essence; then by nine-soul-god placement principle-rising-essence.
sanskrit_cite: saiva mūrtiriti khyātā tārasadbinduhātmikā tato navātmadevena nyāsastattvodayātmakaḥ

plain_english: Limbs and faces of that itself in own places should be placed; then by matrika as before various principle clarity essence.
sanskrit_cite: aṅgavaktrāṇi tasyaiva svasthāneṣu niyojayet atha mātṛkayā prāgvattattattvasphuṭatātmakaḥ

plain_english: On the back, extending through the three regions, one performs the installation of the three principles. Then comes the installation of the eight Ghoras, with the head formed by their feet.
sanskrit_cite: tritattvanyāsatā cāsya pṛṣṭhe kakṣyātrayāgate tato@ghorāṣṭakanyāsaḥ śirastaccaraṇātmakam

plain_english: Then comes the installation of the being of Shiva, joined with one's own body. When this fivefold set has been performed, whatever holds primacy within it should become the main focus.
sanskrit_cite: tato@pi śivasadbhāvanyāsaḥ svāṃgasya saṃyutaḥ ittha kṛte pañcake@sminyattanmukhyatayā bhavet

plain_english: In the sixth installation, one should place the object of contemplation and worship together with its limbs. Therefore, the Lord Ratiśekhara is the one fit to be installed here.
sanskrit_cite: upāsyamarcyaṃ tatsāṅgaṃ ṣaṣṭhe nyāse niyojayet tenātra nyāsayogyo@sau bhagavānratiśekharaḥ

plain_english: The ninefold is to be installed above. When it is given primacy, the other is placed in a different abode. The same rule applies if the being of Bhairava is made primary.
sanskrit_cite: ūrdhve nyāsyo navākhyasya mukhyatve@nyonyadhāmatā evaṃ bhairavasadbhāvanāthe mukhyatayā yadi

plain_english: Ratiśekhara is to be installed beforehand in the place appropriate to what is being worshipped. This is how the tradition was set forth to me in the Śrīpūrva scripture.
sanskrit_cite: upāsyatā tattatsthāna prāṅnyāsyo ratiśekharaḥ itthaṃ śrīpūrvaśāstre me saṃpradāyaṃ nyarūpayat

plain_english: In the procedure of installation, the Lord Śambhu is the deity. How could he be excluded? His limbs also exist and are part of it.
sanskrit_cite: śaṃbhunātho nyāsavidhau devo hi kathamanyathā nyāsa vivarjyate@muṣminnaṅgānyapyasya santi hi

plain_english: The form, emanation, and the three principles, together with the form and limbs, are to be understood as belonging to Shiva with his limbs. The installation is declared to be sixfold.
sanskrit_cite: mūrtiḥ sṛṣṭistritattvaṃ cetyaṣṭau mūrtyaṅgasaṃyutāḥ śivaḥ sāṅgaśca vijñeyo nyāsaḥ ṣoḍhā prakīrtitaḥ

plain_english: Above this, one should then perform the sixfold Shakta installation. First comes Parāparā with her faces, and thus Mālinī at the beginning.
sanskrit_cite: asyopari tataḥ śāktaṃ nyāsaṃ kuryācca ṣaḍvidham parāparāṃ savaktrāṃ prāktataḥ prāgiti mālinīm

plain_english: After that, the triad beginning with Parā is installed in order at the crest, heart, and feet. Then the sequence continues through the head, face, throat, heart, navel, secret place, and thighs.
sanskrit_cite: paścātparāditritayaṃ śikhāhṛtpādagaṃ kramāt tataḥ kavaktrakaṇṭheṣu hṛnnābhīguhya+ūrutaḥ

plain_english: The sequence beginning with Aghorā is placed in the knee and foot. Then come the five limbs of the vidyā. After that, one should invoke the Shakti whose form is the being of the Mother.
sanskrit_cite: jānupāde@pyaghoryādyaṃ tato vidyāṅgapañcakam tatastvāvāhayecchaktiṃ mātṛsadbhāvarūpiṇīm

plain_english: One invokes Yogeśvarī, the supreme, full, steadfast Kālasaṃkarṣiṇī, augmented by the twelve Shaktis of her limbs, faces, and retinue.
sanskrit_cite: yogeśvarīṃ parāṃ pūrṇāṃ kālasaṃkarṣiṇīṃ dhruvām aṅgavaktraparīvāraśaktidvādaśakādhikām

plain_english: At the time of installation, the guru should contemplate according to the aim and practice of the rite. The supreme goddess, abiding in the middle of the triad, is the non-differentiating one.
sanskrit_cite: sādhyānuṣṭhānabhedena nyāsakāle smaredguruḥ paraiva devītritayamadhye yābhedinī sthitā

plain_english: She is proclaimed as the being of unlimited consciousness alone. This is declared in the Sāra scripture and in the Yāmala, and therefore this is how the goddess is understood.
sanskrit_cite: sānavacchedacinmātrasadbhāveyaṃ prakīrtitā sāraśāstre yāmale ca devyāstena prakīrtitaḥ

plain_english: The form with faces, the Shakti, the triad of Shaktis, the group of eight, the five limbs, and the supreme Shakti make up the Shakta installation, which is also sixfold.
sanskrit_cite: mūrtiḥ savaktrā śaktiśca śaktitrayamathāṣṭakam pañcāṅgāni parā śaktirnyāsaḥ śākto@pi ṣaḍvidhaḥ

plain_english: This Yāmala great installation gives the fruits of accomplishment and liberation. But one who seeks liberation alone should first perform the Shakta installation.
sanskrit_cite: yāmalo@yaṃ mahānyāsaḥ siddhimuktiphalapradaḥ muktyekārthī punaḥ pūrvaṃ śāktaṃ nyāsaṃ samācaret

plain_english: The gurus say that for one who desires liberation, the pair of installations described should be performed beginning with the feet, in the order of withdrawal.
sanskrit_cite: guravastvāhuritthaṃ yannyāsadvayamudāhṛtam mumukṣuṇā tu pādādi tatkāryaṃ saṃhṛtikramāt

plain_english: However many divisions are declared as denoting Śambhu, Shakti, and the individual, in all those mantras the installation is proclaimed as sixfold.
sanskrit_cite: yāvantaḥ kīrtitā bhedāḥ śaṃbhuśaktyaṇuvācakāḥ tāvatsvapyeṣu mantreṣu nyāsaḥ ṣoḍhaiva kīrtitaḥ

plain_english: But the mantra that is invoked, endowed with its limbs, should be the sixth. Thus in all cases this installation is stated as sixfold.
sanskrit_cite: kiṃtvāvāhyastu yo mantraḥ sa tatrāṅgasamanvitaḥ ṣaṣṭhaḥ syāditi sarvatra ṣoḍhaivāyamudāhṛtaḥ

plain_english: Afterward come the display of mudrās by body, mind, and speech. There are the five states beginning with waking, and a sixth called the unsurpassed.
sanskrit_cite: mudrāpradarśanaṃ paścātkāyena manasā girā pañcāvasthā jāgradādyāḥ ṣaṣṭhyanuttaranāmikā

plain_english: Because of the six causes, the sixfold selfhood, and the joining of the thirty-six principles, when the sixfold great installation is performed, this whole universe is powerfully brought into unity.
sanskrit_cite: ṣaṭkāraṇaṣaḍātmatvātṣaṭtriṃśattattvayojanam evaṃ ṣoḍhāmahānyāse kṛte viśvamidaṃ haṭhāt

plain_english: Having attained identity in the body, one should reveal a pure emanation. Beginning from the installation of the form, the emanation that has spread forth here is that pure emanation.
sanskrit_cite: dehe tādātmyamāpannaṃ śuddhāṃ sṛṣṭiṃ prakāśayet mūrtinyāsātsamārabhya yā sṛṣṭiḥ prasṛtātra sā

plain_english: By the power and order of the installation, the emanation is brought to non-difference and made pure. Therefore those deluded people who object regarding the shaking off of the burning of bonds are mistaken.
sanskrit_cite: abhedamānīya kṛtā śuddhā nyāsabalakramāt tena ye@codayanmūḍhāḥ pāśadāhavidhūnane

plain_english: When one is established in peaceful Shiva, why would he descend again? Those who ask this are refuted from the outset, for they do not understand the ultimate reality of Śambhu.
sanskrit_cite: kṛte śānte śive rūḍhaḥ punaḥ kimavarohati iti te dūrato dhvastāḥ paramārthaṃ hi śāṃbhavam

plain_english: They do not know, because they are devoid of the essence of the flashing of their own awareness. For this peaceful Shiva is not some differentiated entity.
sanskrit_cite: na vidusta svasaṃvittisphurattāsāravarjitāḥ na khalveṣa śivaḥ śānto nāma kaścidvibhedavān

plain_english: Anything excluded from all other paths is limited somewhere, like a pot. But this consciousness, whose nature is great light, truly expands.
sanskrit_cite: sarvetarādhvavyāvṛtto ghaṭatulyo@sti kutracit mahāprakāśarūpā hi yeyaṃ saṃvidvijṛmbhate

plain_english: That consciousness is Shiva, and Shiva's nature is to appear as all forms. Therefore, through that very manifestation, he expands by his own essence.
sanskrit_cite: sa śivaḥ śivataivāsya vaiśvarūpyāvabhāsitā tathābhāsanayogo@taḥ svarasenāsya jṛmbhate

plain_english: In this manifestation, both non-difference and difference of one's own self appear. When difference expands, maya unfolds, and with it the maya-bound subject comes into play.
sanskrit_cite: bhāsyamāno@tra cābhedaḥ svātmano bheda eva ca bhede vijṛmbhite māyā māyāmāturvijṛmbhate

plain_english: When non-difference expands, that very maya-bound subject unfolds into Shiva-nature. The maya-bound subject attains this through skill gained by practicing identification with that form.
sanskrit_cite: abhede jṛmbhate@syaiva māyāmātuḥ śivātmatā māyāpramātā tadrūpavikalpābhyāsapāṭavāt

plain_english: Shiva alone is declared to be the fruit of that practice, including nyasa and the rest. For just as one becomes shaped by contemplating, 'I am a doer of bad deeds,' so too contemplation determines one's state.
sanskrit_cite: śiva eva tadabhyāsaphalaṃ nyāsādi kīrtitam yathāhi duṣṭakarmāsmītyevaṃ bhāvayatastathā

plain_english: So too, for one who contemplates, 'I am Shiva, I am no other,' the result follows accordingly. This alone is called firmness: when it has gone to the very heart of reflective awareness.
sanskrit_cite: tathā śivo@haṃ nānyo@smītyevaṃ bhāvayatastathā etadevocyate dārḍhyaṃ vimarśahṛdayaṅgamam

plain_english: The non-conceptual state is reached through streams of thought centered on identity with Shiva. Otherwise, how could that pure reality, which lives by the very life of reflective awareness, be approached?
sanskrit_cite: śivaikātmyavikalpaughadvārikā nirvikalpatā anyathā tasya śuddhasya vimarśaprāṇavartinaḥ

plain_english: How could any form of that whose nature is to shine ever remain unexamined by awareness? Therefore, by the power of its sovereign free will, this reality accomplishes even what seems most difficult.
sanskrit_cite: kathaṃ nāmāvimṛṣṭaṃ syādrūpaṃ bhāsanadharmaṇaḥ tenātidurghaṭaghaṭāsvatantrecchāvaśādayam

plain_english: Even though breath, intellect, and the like appear to shine, one should not conceive them as having their own independent nature. On the contrary, their nature is opposite to that of the supremely free self.
sanskrit_cite: bhānapi prāṇabuddhyādiḥ svaṃ tathā na vikalpayet pratyutātisvatantrātmaviparītasvadharmatām

plain_english: If one ascertains these faculties only as perishable and dependent on the Lord, one sinks into a certainty that cuts one off into participation in samsara.
sanskrit_cite: vināśyanīśāyattatvarūpāṃ niścitya majjati tataḥ saṃsārabhāgīyatathāniścayaśātinīm

plain_english: Instead, one should take refuge in a non-conceptual abiding that comes through certainty in the eternal and so forth. But those who are endowed with purity born of the most intense descent of grace are different.
sanskrit_cite: nityādiniścayadvārāmavikalpāṃ sthitiṃ śrayet ye tu tīvratamodriktaśaktinirmalatājuṣaḥ

plain_english: It has been explained that those purified by the most intense grace do not perform initiation and nyasa. But in this way, one who has the universe as his body clearly attains the state of being the universal self.
sanskrit_cite: na te dīkṣāmanunyāsakāriṇaśceti varṇitam evaṃ viśvaśarīraḥ sanviśvātmatvaṃ gataḥ sphuṭam

plain_english: From nyasa alone, the body becomes transformed in that way, and one should worship it with flowers and other offerings. This may be done in detail with separate mantras, or briefly with the root mantra.
sanskrit_cite: nyāsamātrāt tathābhūtaṃ dehaṃ puṣpādinārcayet pṛthaṅmantrairvistareṇa saṃkṣepānmūlamantrataḥ

plain_english: With incense, food offerings, acts of satisfaction, and so on, worship may be done in elaborate or concise form. Because samsara moves in a leftward way, all of this should be done with the left hand.
sanskrit_cite: dhūpanaivedyatṛptyādyaistathā vyāsasamāsataḥ saṃsāravāmācāratvātsarvaṃ vāmakareṇa tu

plain_english: The teacher should also perform the rite of offering with that unimpaired hand. In the revered Matanga and other texts, the word 'left' is said to signify the secret.
sanskrit_cite: kuryāttarpaṇayogaṃ ca daiśikastadanāmayā vāmaśabdena guhyaṃ śrīmataṅgādāvapīritam

plain_english: The mantra practitioner devoted to left practice should perform the worship; this is stated clearly in the revered Bharga-shikha scripture and likewise in the revered Agama teaching.
sanskrit_cite: vāmācāraparo mantrī yāgaṃ kuryāditi sphuṭam śrīmadbhargaśikhāśāstre tathā śrīgamaśāsane

plain_english: Whatever merit there is in all sacred places and whatever fruit there is in all sacrifices, that fruit, O beloved, is multiplied ten million times by offering to the unimpaired one.
sanskrit_cite: sarvatīrtheṣu yatpuṇyaṃ sarvayajñeṣu yatphalam tatphalaṃ koṭiguṇitamanāmātarpaṇātpriye

plain_english: In the revered Nandi-shikha and in the revered Ananda teaching it is said that the ladle should be full, and the spoon should be used in the offering of ghee.
sanskrit_cite: śrīmannandiśikhāyāṃ ca śrīmadānandaśāsane taduktaṃ srukca pūrṇāyāṃ sruvaśvājyāhutau bhavet

plain_english: The rest, including worship, fire offering, recitation, and so on, should be done with the left hand alone. In this way the body becomes filled with bliss and free from turning outward toward everything.
sanskrit_cite: śeṣaṃ vāmakareṇaiva pūjāhomajapādikam evamānandasaṃpūrṇaṃ sarvaunmukhyavivarjitam

plain_english: Having accomplished the body through worship, one should contemplate it as of Shiva-nature. When outward turning toward objects has dissolved and limitation has melted away, this contemplation becomes clear.
sanskrit_cite: yāgena dehaṃ miṣpādya bhāvayeta śivātmakam galite viṣayaunmukhye pārimitye vilāpite

plain_english: When limitation has dissolved, what would remain in the body apart from the essence of Shiva-bliss? The body is filled with the essence of Shiva-bliss and pervaded by the thirty-six principles.
sanskrit_cite: dehe kimavaśiṣyeta śivānandarasādṛte śivānandarasāpūrṇaṃ ṣaṭtriṃśattattvanirbharam
