plain_english: Seeing and worshipping the body day and night, one becomes of Shiva-nature. Such a person is satisfied, resting in the body as the universal self and established in its sign.
sanskrit_cite: dehaṃ divāniśaṃ paśyannarcayansyācchivātmakaḥ viśvātmadehaviśrāntitṛptastalliṅganiṣṭhitaḥ

plain_english: Such a person does not desire external observances like linga vows, sacred places, and similar practices. The rites were taught so that consciousness might come to rest, and for one in whom it already rests, that is enough.
sanskrit_cite: bāhyaṃ liṅgavratakṣetracaryādi nahi vāñchati tāvanmātrāttvaviśrānteḥ saṃvidaḥ kathitāḥ kriyāḥ

plain_english: The higher rites, extending up to external worship, are to be accomplished here for the sake of realizing Shiva-nature. Therefore, the offering vessel should be made as the supreme reality consisting of non-difference from Shiva.
sanskrit_cite: uttarā bāhyayāgāntāḥ sādhyā tvatra śivātmatā tato@rghapātraṃ kartavyaṃ śivābhedamayaṃ param

plain_english: Just as in the body there is a progression from burning to worship, so too the act is full of bliss-essence and satisfies all world-deities.
sanskrit_cite: ānandarasasaṃpūrṇaṃ viśvadaivatatarpaṇam yathaiva dehe dāhādipūjāntaṃ tadvadeva hi

plain_english: Even in the argha vessel, by summary and expansion, which substances are for sacrifice and what argha is, is not declared.
sanskrit_cite: arghapātre@pi kartavyaṃ samāsavyāsayogataḥ kāni dravyāṇi yāgāya ko nvargha iti noditam

plain_english: For one desiring siddhi, the means is indeed the cause in that siddhi; for one desiring liberation, nothing is forbidden and nothing is prescribed.
sanskrit_cite: siddhikāmasya tatsiddhau sādhanaiva hi kāraṇam muktikāmasya no kiṃcinniṣiddhaṃ vihitaṃ ca no

plain_english: Whatever is pleasing is suitable in Shiva-consciousness distinction; having made the argha vessel, sprinkle it with drops and offer flowers and such.
sanskrit_cite: yadeva hṛdyaṃ tadyogyaṃ śivasaṃvidabhedane kṛtvārghapātraṃ tadvipruṭprokṣitaṃ kusumādikam

plain_english: Having made by that, one should worship oneself as supreme Shiva, from fear of confusion of flowers given in argha worship.
sanskrit_cite: kṛtvā ca tena svātmānaṃ pūjayetparamaṃ śivam arghapātrārcanādattapuṣpasaṃkīrṇatābhayāt

plain_english: Do not put a flower in the argha vessel for deity worship; in the argha vessel it becomes nectar-water, and that is worshipped.
sanskrit_cite: nārghapātre@tra kusumaṃ kuryāddevārcanākṛte arghapātre tadamṛtībhūtamambveva pūjitam

plain_english: For satisfaction of mantras and purification of sacrifice substances only; thus, having worshipped the body, one addresses forms empty of prana and intellect.
sanskrit_cite: mantrāṇāṃ tṛptaye yāgadravyaśuddhyai ca kevalam evaṃ dehaṃ pūjayitvā prāṇadhīśūnyavigrahān

plain_english: Worship those who have become mutually identified, in such a Shiva state, when nyasa of prana-support is fashioned by intellect.
sanskrit_cite: anyonyatanmayībhūtān pūjayecchivatādṛśe tatra prāṇāśraye nayāse buddhyā viracite sati

plain_english: From the empty base all is worshipped by one effort; but place the support-power four fingers below the navel.
sanskrit_cite: śūnyādhiṣṭhānataḥ sarvamekayatnena pūjyate nyasyedādhāraśaktiṃ tu nābhyadhaścaturaṅgulām

plain_english: Earth, the ocean of gods, and fire; vessel-form and wind-stalk nature, from the world-thread installation.
sanskrit_cite: dharāṃ surodaṃ tejaśca meyapārapratiṣṭhiteḥ potarūpaṃ marutkandasvabhāvaṃ viśvasūtraṇāt

plain_english: Place four at each finger, sky-womb, slightly all around, pure, essence-like.
sanskrit_cite: pratyekamaṅgulaṃ nyasyeccatuṣkaṃ vyomagarbhakam īṣatsamantādamalamidamāmalasārakam

plain_english: Then make the staff named Ananta up to the uvula, ending in tanmatras and kalas; above that is a knot of night-nature.
sanskrit_cite: tato daṇḍamanantākhyaṃ kalpayellambikāvadhi tanmātrādikalāntaṃ tadūrdhve granthirniśātmakaḥ

plain_english: In that maya-made knot are eight beginning with dharma and adharma; fire and such are maya; its offspring is vibhava, and intellect.
sanskrit_cite: tatra māyāmaye granthau dharmādharmādyamaṣṭakam vahniprāgādi māyā hi tatsūtirvibhavastu dhīḥ

plain_english: Above the maya knot, meditate the four below the trident, of pure-vidya nature, joined with two coverings.
sanskrit_cite: māyāgrantherūrdhvabhūmau triśūlādhaścatuṣkikām śuddhavidyātmikāṃ dhyāyecchadanadvayasaṃyutām

plain_english: That tattva is situated and to be meditated between uvula and brahmarandhra; light-yoga occurs there, with sight, hearing, taste, and such.
sanskrit_cite: tacca tattvaṃ sthitaṃ bhāvyaṃ lambikābrahmarandhrayoḥ prakāśayogo hyatraivaṃ dṛkśrotrarasanādikaḥ

plain_english: Place eighteen shaktis clockwise from the right in the vidya lotus here; that was also said before and is shown again.
sanskrit_cite: dakṣānyāvartato nyasyecchaktīnāṃ navakadvayam vidyāpadme@tra taccoktamapi prāgdarśyate punaḥ

plain_english: Vama, Jyeshtha, Raudri, Kali, Kalabalavikarika, Balamathani, Bhutadamani, and Manonmanika, Shanta; Shakracaparucira may be here.
sanskrit_cite: vāmā jyeṣṭhā raudrī kālī kalabalavikarike balamathanī bhūtadamanī ca manonmanikā śāntā śakracāparuciratra syāt

plain_english: Vibhvi, Jnaptikriti, Iccha, Vagishi, Jvalini, and Vama, Jyeshtha, Raudri—these from the eastern petal, all like time-burning.
sanskrit_cite: vibhvī jñaptikṛtīcchā vāgīśī jvālinī tathā vāmā jyeṣṭhā raudrītyetāḥ prāgdalataḥ kāladahanavatsarvāḥ

plain_english: In the petal-filament centers, remember the sun-moon-fire triad, presided by its own lords Brahma, Vishnu, and Hara.
sanskrit_cite: dalakesaramadhyeṣu sūryendudahanatrayam nijādhipairbrahmaviṣṇuharaiścādhiṣṭhitaṃ smaret

plain_english: The form beyond maya of Brahma and others was previously stated; this seat is indeed that, not smeared with maya collyrium.
sanskrit_cite: māyottīrṇaṃ hi yadrūpaṃ brahmādīnāṃ puroditam āsanaṃ tvetadeva syānnatu māyāñjanāñjitam

plain_english: Above Rudra place Ishvara god, and above that Sadasiva; he is called Mahapreta in the scriptures.
sanskrit_cite: rudrordhve ceśvaraṃ devaṃ tadūrdhve ca sadāśivam nyasyetsa ca mahāpreta iti śāstreṣu bhaṇyate

plain_english: Mahapreta, by pervading all tattvas, is absorbed from awakening and excellent going, and would not go downward.
sanskrit_cite: samastatattvavyāptṛtvānmahāpretaḥ prabodhataḥ prakarṣagamanāccaiṣa līno yannādharaṃ vrajet

plain_english: All lords of vidya and avidya, having gone higher and higher and become Sadasiva, then resort to supreme Shiva.
sanskrit_cite: vidyāvidyeśinaḥ sarve hyuttarottaratāṃ gatāḥ sadāśivībhūya tataḥ paraṃ śivamupāśritāḥ

plain_english: Therefore Sadasiva is always upward-gazing luminous self; he is thin due to measurability and weakness, a preta from loud laughter and such.
sanskrit_cite: ataḥ sadāśivo nityamūrdhvadṛgbhāsvarātmakaḥ kṛśo meyatvadaurbalyātpreto@ṭṭahasanāditaḥ

plain_english: Remember the sound-end self, pervaded by Śakti and bright in mind, risen from the navel and exited through the three crown openings.
sanskrit_cite: tasya nābhyutthitaṃ mūrdharandhratrayavinirgatam nādāntātma smarecchaktivyāpinīsamanojjvalam

plain_english: Three spokes, twelve-ended, there also beyond-mind three; of white lotuses, this is the thirty-seven-self seat.
sanskrit_cite: arātrayaṃ dviṣaṭkāntaṃ tatrāpyaunmanasaṃ trayam paṅkajānāṃ sitaṃ saptatriṃśadātmedamāsanam

plain_english: Here all principles with distinction-breath; from that, distinct as seat, indeed the object of consciousness is remembered.
sanskrit_cite: atra sarvāṇi tattvāni bhedaprāṇāni yattataḥ āsanatvena bhinnaṃ hi saṃvido viṣayaḥ smṛtaḥ

plain_english: These very principles are dissolved in supreme Bhairava; then by identity they are created in distinction-deva-worship-joining.
sanskrit_cite: etānyeva tu tattvāni līnāni parabhairave tādātmyenātha sṛṣṭāni bhidevārcyatvayojane

plain_english: Having Śrī Bhairava knowledge-unity gain freedom, these very principles attain worshipper-hood enough.
sanskrit_cite: śrīmadbhairavabodhaikyalābhasvātantryavanti tu etānyeva tu tattvāni pūjakatvaṃ prayāntyalam

plain_english: The worshipper is supreme-principle self; the worshipped principle is supreme-inferior, and because created, the inferior principle-net is the seat-state foundation.
sanskrit_cite: pūjakaḥ paratattvātmā pūjyaṃ tattvaṃ parāparam sṛṣṭatvādaparaṃ tattvajālamāsanatāspadam

plain_english: In Siddhānta it ends at vidyā-kalā; in left-right scriptures at Sadāśiva; in Mata Yāmala at Samanā.
sanskrit_cite: vidyākalāntaṃ siddhānte vāmadakṣiṇaśāstrayoḥ sadāśivāntaṃ samanāparyantaṃ matayāmale

plain_english: Ending at unmanā, here called this supreme seat; having worshipped the seat, the worshipped guru line is as Bhāvin.
sanskrit_cite: unmanāntamihākhyātamityetatparamāsanam arcayitvāsanaṃ pūjyā gurupaṅktistu bhāvivat

plain_english: In that seat, formerly embodied, with half-syllable, two; place as pervader-ness, thus said in Siddha Yogīśvarī Mata.
sanskrit_cite: tatrāsane purā mūrtibhūtāṃ sārdhākṣarāṃ dvayīm nyasyedvyāptṛtayetyuktaṃ siddhayogīśvarīmate

plain_english: Worship Sadāśiva, great preta image, with half-syllable, as supreme above, with incense, flowers, etc., thus.
sanskrit_cite: sadāśivaṃ mahāpretaṃ mūrtiṃ sārdhākṣarāṃ yajet paratvena parāmūrdhve gandhapuṣpādibhistviti

plain_english: Imagine the vidyā-image, then self-named, second; in the middle Bhairava true-being, on the right Rati-crest.
sanskrit_cite: vidyāmūrtimathātmākhyāṃ dvitīyāṃ parikalpayet madhye bhairavasadbhāvaṃ dakṣiṇe ratiśekharam

plain_english: Nine-self; on the left that devī-like Bhairava triad; in the middle supreme full-moon image; on the right again.
sanskrit_cite: navātmānaṃ vāmatastaddevīvadbhairavatrayam madhye parāṃ pūrṇacandrapratimāṃ dakṣiṇe punaḥ

plain_english: The higher-lower form is red and slightly pointed, not terrifying; the lower form on the left horn is terrifying and black-tawny.
sanskrit_cite: parāparāṃ raktavarṇāṃ kiṃcidagrāṃ na bhīṣaṇām aparāṃ vāmaśṛṅge tu bhīṣaṇāṃ kṛṣṇapiṅgalām

plain_english: After placement is done in the body as before, twofold and sixfold, one should then imagine the fitting imagined form of these.
sanskrit_cite: prāgvaddvidhātra ṣoḍhaiva nyāso dehe yathā kṛtaḥ tataḥ sāṃkalpikaṃ yuktaṃ vapurāsāṃ vicintayet

plain_english: According to action difference, forms with two, four, or six arms and so on bear skull, trident, club, boon, fear, pot, and so on.
sanskrit_cite: kṛtyabhedānusāreṇa dvicatuḥṣaḍbhujādikam kapālaśūlakhaṭvāṅgavarābhayaghaṭādikam

plain_english: One imagines because of variegated left-right placement, since in reality these goddesses are universal forms of consciousness-nature.
sanskrit_cite: vāmadakṣiṇasaṃsthānacitratvātparikalpayet vastuto viśvarūpāstā devyo bodhātmikā yataḥ

plain_english: Their essence is unlimited consciousness alone, for liberation; then all limbs, faces, and so on, world-guardians, weapons, last.
sanskrit_cite: anavacchinnacinmātrasārāḥ syurapavṛktaye sarvaṃ tato@ṅgavaktrādi lokapālāstrapaścimam

plain_english: In the middle the goddess-named worshipful triad becomes and is worshiped, then from the middle-seated mass of consciousness and eternal unity.
sanskrit_cite: madhye devyabhidhā pūjyā trayaṃ bhavati pūjitam tato madhyagatāttasmādbodharāśeḥ sadaivatāt

plain_english: The emanated limbs and so on are worshipful and spark-natured, separate; the goddess going in the middle is indeed she, formed of true being.
sanskrit_cite: aṅgādi niḥsṛtaṃ pūjyaṃ visphuliṅgātmakaṃ pṛthak madhyagā kila yā devī saiva sadbhāvarūpiṇī

plain_english: The time-drawing goddess is fierce, peaceful, and mixed everywhere; in the siddha tantra the supreme goddess with one syllable is thus praised.
sanskrit_cite: kālasaṃkarṣiṇī ghorā śāntā miśrā ca sarvataḥ siddhātantre ca saikārṇā parā devīti kīrtitā

plain_english: The supreme mother goddess Mālinī, middle-risen, is in the middle; one should place there the all-letters-composed supreme sun-radiance.
sanskrit_cite: parā tu mātṛkā devī mālinī madhyagoditā madhye nyasyetsūryaruciṃ sarvākṣaramayīṃ parām

plain_english: At her crest-tip is indeed the one-syllabled; her limbs and so on are thus; then the universe emerged and is worshiped in south and north.
sanskrit_cite: tasyāḥ śikhāgre tvaikārṇāṃ tasyāścāṅgādikaṃ tviti tato viśvaṃ viniṣkrāntaṃ pūjitaṃ dakṣiṇottare

plain_english: It may indeed be worshiped by that; once in the middle one should worship, as said in the Shridevi tantra sacrifice named Damara.
sanskrit_cite: syādeva pūjitaṃ tena sakṛnmadhye prapūjayet śrīdevyāyāmale coktaṃ yāge ḍāmarasaṃjñite

plain_english: At the nose-tip is threefold time; the time-drawing goddess, always situated in the mouth and calculating breath and inbreath, draws in the heart.
sanskrit_cite: nāsāgre trividhaṃ kālaṃ kālasaṃkarṣiṇī sadā mukhasthā śvāsaniḥśvāsakalanī hṛdi karṣati

plain_english: Through inhalations and retentions it holds and seizes time, but through exhalation it completely seizes all time; rising with the exhalation, it does so in an instant.
sanskrit_cite: pūrakaiḥ kumbhakairdhatte grasate recakena tu kālaṃ saṃgrasate sarvaṃ recakenotthitā kṣaṇāt

plain_english: The supreme will-power, by name the awakener of the three powers, is to be worshipped; it draws in all and shatters the very support of time.
sanskrit_cite: icchāśaktiḥ parā nāmnā śaktitritayabodhinī yājyā karṣati yatsarvaṃ kālādhāraprabhañjanam

plain_english: O Shiva, the powers of seeing, action, and will, when engaged in the gross and subtle cutting of the knowable, become in order the sakala and the pralayākala.
sanskrit_cite: iha kila dṛkkarmecchāḥ śiva uktāstāstu vedyakhaṇḍanake sthūle sūkṣme kramaśaḥ sakalapralayākalau bhavataḥ

plain_english: When pure but asleep, the powers become the knowledge-limited state; when awakened, knowing some divided knowables, they are called mantras.
sanskrit_cite: śuddhā eva tu suptā jñānākalatāṃ gatāḥ prabuddhāstu pravibhinnakatipayātmakavedyavido mantra ucyante

plain_english: When the whole knowable is divided, the lords of mantras and the great lords arise; when it is both divided and undivided, the path up to Sadāśiva arises, culminating in the supreme Lord.
sanskrit_cite: bhinne tvakhile vedye mantreśāstanmaheśāstu bhinnābhinne tadiyān suśivānto@dhvoditaḥ prete

plain_english: As the expansion of difference dissolves, those powers gradually expand and, mutually mixed, become the triad of tvaras; then, with difference dissolved, they go beyond it.
sanskrit_cite: tā eva galati bhedaprasare kramaśo vikāsamāyāntyaḥ anyonyāsaṃkīrṇāstvarātrayaṃ galitabhedikāstu tataḥ

plain_english: The triad of lotuses together with unmanā becomes the seat, as the powers take it up out of a desire to cut away their mutual difference.
sanskrit_cite: padmatrayyaunmanasī tadidaṃ syādāsanatvena tā evānyonyātmakabhedāvacchedanājihāsutayā

plain_english: Indeed, the divisions of power, its possessor, and so forth become worthy of worship, because from the very first point of the dissolution of difference each bears its own proper form.
sanskrit_cite: kila śaktitadvadādiprabhidā pūjyatvamāyātāḥ bhedagalanādyakoṭerārabhya yato nijaṃ nijaṃ rūpam

plain_english: They bear a threefoldness, and that threefoldness of theirs is clearly perceived because of the possible impurity of the knowable and the mutual mixture they acquire.
sanskrit_cite: bibhrati tāstu tritvaṃ tāsāṃ sphuṭameva lakṣyeta saṃbhāvyavedyakāluṣyayogato@nyonyalabdhasaṃkarataḥ

plain_english: Not arriving at a clearly threefold state as before, but ready to devour the very act of cutting mutual difference, that consciousness, whose essence is freedom alone, is declared to be Kālakarṣiṇī.
sanskrit_cite: prāk prasphuṭaṃ tribhāvaṃ nāgacchannatra tu tathā na anyonyātmakabhedāvacchedanakalanasaṃgrasiṣṇutayā svātantryamātrasārā saṃvitsā kālakarṣiṇī kathitā

plain_english: She again draws time back from herself and also projects it outward; therefore she is declared Saṃkarṣiṇī, and this is her true being among these Mothers.
sanskrit_cite: saiva ca bhūyaḥ svasmātsaṃkarṣati kālamiha bahiṣkurute saṃkarṣiṇīti kathitā mātṛṣveteṣu sadbhāvaḥ

plain_english: True nature, being, and attainment among the Mothers are to be understood in this way; in those world-generating powers, the supreme reality is indeed freedom alone.
sanskrit_cite: tattvaṃ sattā prāptirmātṛṣu meyo@nayā saṃśca viśvajananīṣu śaktiṣu paramārtho hi svatantratāmātram

plain_english: This worshippable reality, consisting of willing, knowing, and acting, is worthy of worship because it is unlimited; even all directions of limitation are gathered within it.
sanskrit_cite: eṣaṇavidikriyātmakametatpūjyaṃ yato@navacchinnam yasminsarvāvacchedadiśo@pi syuḥ samākṣiptāḥ

plain_english: Here the non-conceptual does not attain worshippability, nor does a mere single concept where many attributes are involved; therefore the attribute that gathers in that many attributes is required.
sanskrit_cite: avikalpamiha na yāti hi pūjyatvaṃ naca vikalpa ekatra bahavo dharmāstasmād yo dharmastāvato dharmān

plain_english: That which draws in all attributes is established there as supreme, while all others stand lower; such is the principle of supreme Bhairava worship in the great rite of the revered Ḍāmara.
sanskrit_cite: ākṣipati tatra rūḍhaḥ sarvotkṛṣṭo@dharasthitāstvanye iti bhairavaparapūjātattvaṃ śrīḍāmare mahāyāge

plain_english: The glorious Śambhu himself, well pleased, taught this to me: in the external rite one should worship also in the triad of lotuses.
sanskrit_cite: svayameva suprasannaḥ śrīmān śaṃbhurmamādikṣat bāhyayāge tu padmānāṃ tritaye@pi prapūjayet

plain_english: The teaching of the instructors is that the retinue multitude ends with the weapon mantra, and the fivefold group of vidyā-limbs is placed in the directions of Agni, Īśa, the demons, Vāyu, and the intermediate quarters.
sanskrit_cite: astrāntaṃ parivāraughamiti no daiśikāgamaḥ agnīśarakṣovāyvantadikṣu vidyāṅgapañcakam

plain_english: Here one should likewise place the limbs of Śakti and the limbs of Śiva; again in the pair, place the weapon mantra in the four directions, and in the middle place the mantra called Locana.
sanskrit_cite: śaktyaṅgāni śivāṅgāni tathaivātra punardvaye astraṃ nyasyeccaturdikkaṃ madhye locanasaṃjñakam

plain_english: On the eight petals place a pair of octads beginning with Aghorā, according to its own tradition; likewise arrange groups of twelve, six, and four, mixed and distributed two by two.
sanskrit_cite: patrāṣṭake@ṣṭakayugamaghorādeḥ svayāmalam tathā dvādaśakaṃ ṣaṭkaṃ catuṣkaṃ miśritaṃ dviśaḥ

plain_english: One should worship in every way as a doubled enclosure; then, in order, worship the world guardians with their weapons in their own ten directions.
sanskrit_cite: sarvaśo dviguṇādītthamāvṛtitvena pūjayet lokapālāṃstataḥ sāstrānsvadikṣu daśasu kramāt

plain_english: Thus, abiding in identity with the goddesses up to the trident, standing here and offering the universe, one should satisfy the host of deities.
sanskrit_cite: itthaṃ triśūlaparyantadevītādātmyavṛttitaḥ tiṣṭhannatrārpayanviśvaṃ tarpayeddevatāgaṇam

plain_english: Then one should perform recitation, ten times for each mantra; because each is threefold in nature and yet non-different, this holds in all respects.
sanskrit_cite: tato japaṃ prakurvīta pratimantraṃ dvipañcadhā ekaikasya tryātmakatvādabhedāccāpi sarvaśaḥ

plain_english: Remembering the mantra circle like fire in the navel, heart, throat, palate, and upper center, one should there burn the universe and accomplish the oblation.
sanskrit_cite: nābhihṛtkaṇṭhatālūrdhvakuṇḍe jvalanavatsmaran mantracakraṃ tatra viśvaṃ jvahvansaṃpādayeddhutim

plain_english: When the act of initiation is to be performed, by whichever path the teacher desires to carry it out, he should first and primarily apply that path in the body.
sanskrit_cite: dīkṣākarmaṇi kartavye dīkṣāṃ yenādhvanā guruḥ cikīrṣurdeha evādau bhūyastaṃ mukhyato@rpayet

plain_english: Remembering the trident extending from the root up to the twelve-end-point, with its tip forward, and reaching the tip of the circle of goddesses while abandoning sequence, one attains the state of moving in space.
sanskrit_cite: dvādaśāntamidaṃ prāgraṃ triśūlaṃ mūlataḥ smaran devīcakrāgragaṃ tyaktakramaḥ khecaratāṃ vrajet

plain_english: This khecarī fills everything from the root-support up to the top of the space at the end of the twelve; she is called khecarī because she moves and abides in space and feeds on the nectar of space.
sanskrit_cite: mūlādhārāddviṣaṭkāntavyomāgrāpūraṇātmikā khecarīyaṃ khasaṃcārasthitibhyāṃ khāmṛtāśanāt

plain_english: From that Śāmbhava trident one should reduce by four finger-widths for the Śākta, and from that again for the Āṇava; thus that triad of tridents is established.
sanskrit_cite: amuṣmācchāmbhavācchūlāddhrāsayeccaturaṅgulam śākte tato@pyāṇave tattriśūlatritayaṃ sthitam

plain_english: For one whose self is offered to the higher and higher circles of goddesses on that triad of tridents, what is not born, what is not known, or what is not done?
sanskrit_cite: tattriśūlatrayordhvordhvadevīcakrārpitātmakaḥ kiṃ kiṃ na jāyate kiṃ vā na vetti na karoti vā

plain_english: Alternatively, one should worship each single goddess or each mantra in a lotus, varying the worship according to paired union, limbs, faces, and other options of being or non-being.
sanskrit_cite: ekaikāmathavā devīṃ mantraṃ vā padmagaṃ yajet yāmalaikyāṅgavaktrādisadasattāvikalpataḥ

plain_english: In this way, having made one's own consciousness Śiva from the level of breath up to the level of space through the yoga of worship, one should then perform the external rite.
sanskrit_cite: itthaṃ prāṇādvyomapadaparyantaṃ cetanaṃ nijam śivībhāvyārcanāyogāttato bāhyaṃ vidhiṃ caret

plain_english: When external worship is made primary and is aimed at powers and the like, internal worship is for purification; otherwise the worshipper remains a bound soul.
sanskrit_cite: bahiryāgasya mukhyatve siddhyādiparikalpite antaryāgaḥ saṃskriyāyai hyanyathārcayitā paśuḥ

plain_english: But whoever is turned away from powers and the like and worships the Lord outwardly for the sake of rising into the inner great worship, that person is fulfilled by that very means.
sanskrit_cite: yastu siddhyādivimukhaḥ sa bahiryajati prabhum antarmahāyāgarūḍhyai tayaivāsau kṛtārthakaḥ

plain_english: After performing the inner worship, one should take grain and the like consecrated with the weapon-mantra, throw it in the directions to remove obstacles, and then gather it back toward the Īśāna direction.
sanskrit_cite: kṛtvāntaryāgamādāya dhānyādyastreṇa mantritam dikṣu kṣipedvighnanude saṃhṛtyaiśīṃ diśaṃ nayet

plain_english: Inspection, sprinkling, striking and nourishing, and covering are purifications that are common in the doctrine of Triśiras.
sanskrit_cite: nirīkṣaṇaṃ prokṣaṇaṃ ca tāḍanāpyāyane tathā viguṇṭhanaṃ ca saṃskārāḥ sādhārāstriśiromate

plain_english: One should consecrate cow urine, cow dung, curd, milk, and ghee with the faces ending in the upper one and with the six limbs, and sprinkle with this kuśa-water.
sanskrit_cite: gomūtragomayadadhikṣīrājyaṃ mantrayenmukhaiḥ ūrdhvāntairaṅgaṣaṭkena kuśāmbvetena cokṣayet

plain_english: One should sprinkle the ground and set aside the remainder of the pañcagavya for the disciple; where the five cow products are in this kuśa-water, that is called pañcagavya.
sanskrit_cite: bhūmiṃ śeṣaṃ ca śiṣyārthaṃ sthāpayetpañcagavyakam pañca gavyāni yatrāsminkuśāmbuni taducyate

plain_english: In the scripture, pañcagavya-water is said to remove external impurity; for when ordinary impurity has been removed, one may then deal with the inner impurity.
sanskrit_cite: pañcagavyaṃ jalaṃ śāstre bāhyāśuddhivimardakam laukikyāmaviśuddhau hi mṛditāyāmathāntarīm

plain_english: To burn away impurity, one must resort to non-ordinary means such as mantra; one should remember the goddess, ending with phāṭ, who extends from earth up to Śiva.
sanskrit_cite: aśuddhiṃ dagdhumāstheyaṃ mantrādi yadalaukikam phādināntāṃ smareddevīṃ pṛthivyādiśivāntagām

plain_english: One should throw a handful of flowers into the middle and likewise offer incense, fragrance, liquor, and so on in the center of the worship-ground; by that the support is quickly empowered.
sanskrit_cite: puṣpāñjaliṃ kṣipenmadhye dhūpagandhāsavādi ca tathaiva dadyādyāgaukomadhye tenāśu vigraham

plain_english: The entire circle of deities is conceived as presiding there, on the stalk of Ananta, on the petals beginning with Dharma, and on the pericarp of true knowledge.
sanskrit_cite: samastaṃ devatācakramadhiṣṭhātṛ prakalpyate anantanāle dharmādipatre sadvaidyakarṇike

plain_english: In the sixfold arising, one should worship Gaṇeśa of Īśāna, placed there, with fragrance, flowers, and the like for the calming of obstacles; having worshipped him, one should dismiss him.
sanskrit_cite: ṣaḍutthe gandhapuṣpādyairgaṇeśaṃ hyaiśagaṃ yajet atthitaṃ vighnasaṃśāntyai pūjayitvā visarjayet

plain_english: After the missing portion of the text: then one should take the jar, filled with supremely fragrant liquid substances.
The jar, worshipped and anointed with the root mantra, should be consecrated one hundred times; if the weapon-worship was not done earlier, the water-pot should be consecrated with the sword-mantra.
sanskrit_cite: pūjitaṃ carcitaṃ mūlamanunā mantrayecchatam asinā karkarīṃ pūrvamastrayāgo na cetkṛtaḥ

plain_english: One should worship that jar in the Īśāna direction together with the vessel placed on its left; then, taking position in the solar direction, one should worship the world-lords together with their weapons.
sanskrit_cite: tamaiśānyāṃ yajetkumbhaṃ vāmasthakalaśānvitam tataḥ sauradigāśrityā sāstrāṃllokeśvarānyajet

plain_english: After worshipping them with offerings of fragrance, flowers, and so on according to rule and preceded by mantra, the disciple, holding the sword-vessel in hand, pours down a stream.
sanskrit_cite: gandhapuṣpopahārādyairvidhinā mantrapūrvakam tataḥ śiṣyo@sikalaśīhasto dhārāṃ prapātayan

plain_english: The guru, holding the jar in hand, should follow while saying this: 'O Śakra, by you, in your own direction, obstacles must be calmed.'
sanskrit_cite: guruṇā kumbhahastenānuvrajyo vadatā tvidam bho bhoḥ śakra tvayā svasyāṃ diśi vighnapraśāntaye

plain_english: One must remain attentive until the end of the rite, by Śiva's command; but in a three-syllable name mostly belonging to Nirṛti, only a single 'bhoḥ' should be used.
sanskrit_cite: sāvadhānena karmāntaṃ bhavitavyaṃ śivājñayā tryakṣare nirṛtiprāye nāmni bhoḥśabdamekakam

plain_english: One should remove it because this mantra is spoken as bound by meter; then that jar should be placed in the Īśāna direction upon the scattered offerings.
sanskrit_cite: apāsayedyato mantraśchandobaddho@yamīritaḥ tata aiśyāṃ diśi sthāpyaḥ sa kumbho vikiropari

plain_english: Now the weapon-vessel should be placed in the south, in relation to the pot, and the group of mantras, strengthened by absorption in the pot's water, is to be used.
sanskrit_cite: dakṣiṇe cāstravārdhānī sthāpyā kumbhasya sāṃpratam kumbhasthāmbusamāpattivṛṃhitaṃ mantravṛndakam

plain_english: Meditating on the mantra-group as pure light, he should nourish the whole rite; therefore the guru should worship the entire assembly of mantras in the pot.
sanskrit_cite: tejomātrātmanā dhyātaṃ sarvamāpyāyayedvidhim ataḥ kumbhe mantragaṇaṃ sarvaṃ saṃpūjayedguruḥ

plain_english: Using the previous method, he should employ the weapon-mantra in the karkarī vessel to drive away obstacles; then the guru should worship in the middle of the house on a fragrant diagram.
sanskrit_cite: pūrveṇa vidhināstraṃ ca karkaryāṃ vighnanudyajet madhyegṛhaṃ tato gandhamaṇḍale pūjayedguruḥ

plain_english: He may worship the mantra-deity as the triad, or in a yāmala form, or as a single unity; then, for the fire rite, he should prepare the fire-pit.
sanskrit_cite: trikaṃ yāmalataikyābhyāmekaṃ vā mantradaivatam agnikāryavidhānāya tataḥ kuṇḍaṃ prakalpayet

plain_english: Having made a ladle or spoon according to enjoyment or liberation, there are triads of gods, powers, and yantras.

plain_english: That same person, knowing the kinds of mantras and the truth of recitation, fire-offering, and the rest, is consecrated first with the liberation vessel and then with the one called Īśvara.
sanskrit_cite: sa eva mantrajātijño japahomāditattvavit nirvāṇakalaśenādau tata īśvarasaṃjñinā

plain_english: When consecrated he becomes a sādhaka, and at the end of enjoyment he dissolves into the supreme; endowed with these qualities, one is initiated in the teaching of Śiva.
sanskrit_cite: abhiṣiktaḥ sādhakaḥ syādbhogānte@sya pare layaḥ etairguṇaiḥ samāyukto dīkṣitaḥ śivaśāsane

plain_english: One who knows the four-part scriptures, is devoted to the eighteen tantras, and knows the ten tantras and the higher path is appointed as an ācārya.
sanskrit_cite: catuṣpātsaṃhitābhijñastantrāṣṭādaśatatparaḥ daśatantrātimārgajña ācāryaḥ sa vidhīyate

plain_english: In the consecration rite, the best of gurus should perform for the ācārya the joining that begins from earth and ends in liberation.
sanskrit_cite: pṛthivīmāditaḥ kṛtvā nirvāṇānte@sya yojanām abhiṣekavidhau kuryādācāryasya gurūttamaḥ

plain_english: By these statements it is said that the samaya-initiate, like a prince, would be authorized everywhere in the three stages beginning with the son stage.
sanskrit_cite: etairvākyairidaṃ coktaṃ samayī rājaputravat sarvatraivādhikārī syātputrakādipadatraye

plain_english: A son-initiate may be authorized in teacherhood if his joining is equal, but he is not authorized in sādhana when the joining is different.
sanskrit_cite: putrako daiśikatve tu tulyayojaniko bhavet adhikārī sa na punaḥ sādhane bhinnayojane

plain_english: In this tantra, the ācārya is one who has obtained the higher rites through the sequence beginning with samaya; never a Buddhist, Vaiṣṇava, or the like.
sanskrit_cite: etattantre samayyādikramādāptottarakriyaḥ ācāryo na punarbauddhavaiṣṇavādiḥ kadācana

plain_english: Thus what arose by context has been settled, and now the main topic is taken up again: having performed the Śiva-hand rite, by that the disciple's bonds are burned away.
sanskrit_cite: evaṃ prasaṅgānnirṇītaṃ prakṛtaṃ tu nirūpyate śivahastavidhiṃ kṛtvā tena saṃpluṣṭapāśakam

plain_english: Having brought the disciple, through meditative absorption, to the point of rest, the guru then places that child-disciple in the vessel, in the weapon-vessel, in the fire, and in his own self.
sanskrit_cite: śiṣyaṃ vidhāya viśrāntiparyantaṃ dhyānayogataḥ tataḥ kumbhe@strakalaśe vahnau svātmani taṃ śiśum

plain_english: He should have the disciple make prostration, then cast an offering to the beings and Mothers; then, having worshipped Śaṃkara, he should prepare a bed consecrated with the weapon-mantra.
sanskrit_cite: praṇāmaṃ kārayetpaścādbhūtamātṛbaliṃ kṣipet tataḥ śaṃkaramabhyarcya śayyāmastrābhimantritām

plain_english: Having placed the disciple on that bed and installed the mantras, the guru establishes rest in the disciple's heart-wheel and then goes to his twelve-end.
sanskrit_cite: kṛtvāsyāṃ śiṣyamāropya nyastamantraṃ vidhāya ca śiṣyahṛccakraviśrāntiṃ kṛtvā taddvādaśāntagaḥ

plain_english: Through the arising of the twelve vowels the net of kalās becomes diminished; then, on entry, he becomes bright with the sixteen kalās gathered together.
sanskrit_cite: bhavetkṣīṇakalājālaḥ svaradvādaśakodayāt tataḥ praveśapracitakalāṣoḍaśakojjvalaḥ

plain_english: As the full moon of his own consciousness, he should rest in the heart of the child-disciple until the rising, and then go to the twelve-end.
sanskrit_cite: saṃpūrṇasvātmaciccandro viśrāmyeddhṛdaye śiśoḥ svayaṃ vyutthānaparyantaṃ dvādaśāntaṃ tato vrajet

plain_english: He should enter the heart-wheel again in this way; this is the sequence of the sleep rite. When sleep has come, this disciple perceives the stainless moon and sun.
sanskrit_cite: punarviśecca hṛccakramitthaṃ nidrāvidhikramaḥ āyātanidraḥ śiṣyo@sau nirmalau śaśibhāskarau

plain_english: In the heart-wheel he forcibly joins together the full and the thin moon and sun, and he truly sees the light of the forcibly stainless moon and sun.
sanskrit_cite: hṛccakre pratisaṃdhatte balātpūrṇakṛśātmakau haṭhanirmalacandrārkaprakāśaḥ satyamīkṣate

plain_english: He sees a dream that clearly reveals future good and other outcomes; and it is taught that, having meditated on the full and the thin in the domain of the twelve, this occurs.
sanskrit_cite: svapnaṃ bhāviśubhānyatvasphuṭībhāvanakovidam uktaṃ ca pūrṇāṃ ca kṛśāṃ dhyātvā dvādaśagocare

plain_english: Entering the heart, meditate; the sleeping child, with the guru worshipping Shankara, attains freedom in temple sleep.
sanskrit_cite: praviśya hṛdaye dhyāye tsuptaḥ svācchandyamāpnuyāt āyātanidre ca śiśau gururabhyarcya śaṅkaram

plain_english: Eat the offering with a friend, then clean the teeth, and sleep with mind fixed in the heart wheel by mantra rays.
sanskrit_cite: caruṃ bhuñjīta sasakhā tato@dyāddantadhāvanam svapyācca mantraraśmīddhahṛccakrārpitamānasaḥ

plain_english: In the morning the guru, having completed daily worship of Shankara, knows the dream-seen meanings of disciple and self from strength and weakness.
sanskrit_cite: prātarguruḥ kṛtāśeṣanityo@bhyarcitaśaṃkaraḥ śiṣyātmanoḥ svapnadṛṣṭāvarthau vitte balābalāt

plain_english: Self-seen strength is not other through awakening excess; in knowledge equality, dream equality would again arise between guru and disciple.
sanskrit_cite: svadṛṣṭaṃ balavannānyatsaṃbodhodrekayogataḥ bodhasāmye punaḥ svapnasāmyaṃ syādguruśiṣyayoḥ

plain_english: God, fire, guru, worship cause and utensils are pleasing; woman, wine drinking, and eating of uncooked meat also appear.
sanskrit_cite: devāgnigurutatpūjākāraṇopaskarādikam hṛdyā strī madyapānaṃ cāpyāmamāṃsasya bhakṣaṇam

plain_english: Blood drinking, head cutting, smearing with blood, feces, and urine, and riding pleasing vehicles such as mountain, horse, and elephant.
sanskrit_cite: raktapānaṃ śiraśchedo raktaviṇmūtralepanam parvatāśvagajaprāyahṛdyayugyādhirohaṇam

plain_english: For pleasure it would even be; mostly that is declared auspicious; announce it for growth of satisfaction, for joy indeed is the supreme fruit.
sanskrit_cite: yatprītyai syādapi prāyastattacchubhamudāhṛtam taṃ khyāpayettuṣṭivṛddhyai hlādo hi paramaṃ phalam

plain_english: Therefore other inauspicious signs there; from homa of eight hundred, inauspicious is not inauspicious; thus the guru tells the disciples.
sanskrit_cite: ato@nyadaśubhaṃ tatra homo@ṣṭaśatako@strataḥ aśubhaṃ nāśubhamiti śiṣyebhyo kathayedguruḥ

plain_english: Indeed great effort arises to cut rooted doubt; but for those whose doubt dissolves, dream-power arises.
sanskrit_cite: rūḍhāṃ hi śaṅkāṃ vicchettuṃ yatnaḥ saṃghaṭate mahān yeṣāṃ tu śaṅkāvilayasteṣāṃ svapnavaśotthitam

plain_english: Nothing auspicious or inauspicious would be; if thus, from variegation power the sattva self clearly sees from sign only.
sanskrit_cite: śubhāśubhaṃ na kiṃcitsyāt syuścetthaṃ citratāvaśāt sphuṭaṃ paśyati sattvātmā rājaso liṅgamātrataḥ

plain_english: Nothing tamasic is his pleasure, pain, auspiciousness, or inauspiciousness; indeed here, how would the one named tamasic be fit in the rite?
sanskrit_cite: na kiṃcittāmasastasya sukhaduḥkhācchubhāśubham nanvatra tāmaso nāma kathaṃ yogyo vidhau bhavet

plain_english: Let no one dispute anywhere indeed; quality is present; even all sattvic action in eating, if tamasic.
sanskrit_cite: maiva mā vigrahaṃ kaścitkvacitkasyāpi vai guṇaḥ sarvasāttvikaceṣṭo@pi bhojane yadi tāmasaḥ

plain_english: Then what is low, or high is the opposite; even arrived power descent and initiation depend on quality state.
sanskrit_cite: kiṃ tataḥ so@dhamaḥ kivāpyutkṛṣṭastadviparyayaḥ āyātaśaktipāto@pi dīkṣito@pi guṇasthiteḥ

plain_english: The variegated self would indeed be composed in chief purpose; then the guru teaches the child mantra-preceded deity worship.
sanskrit_cite: vicitrātmā bhavedeva mukhye tvarthe samāhitaḥ tato guruḥ śiśormantrapūrvakaṃ devatārcanam

plain_english: He would teach and do that, purify him; then the composed guru addresses six places from the heart, brahma and others.
sanskrit_cite: deśayetsa ca tatkuryātsaṃskuryāttaṃ tato guruḥ hṛdādicakraṣaṭkasthānbrahmādīn ṣaṭ samāhitaḥ

plain_english: He would touch the child's breath function; each of eight purifications, purified by knowledge-touch, extends to the heart-first twelve end.
sanskrit_cite: spṛśecchiśoḥ prāṇavṛttyā pratyekaṃ cāṣṭa saṃskriyāḥ hṛdayādidviṣaṭkāntaṃ bodhasparśapavitritaḥ

plain_english: By destruction of faults from food, seed, state, and so on, one becomes twice-born; full of vasu-veda-named purification, thus the twice-born stands.
sanskrit_cite: āhārabījabhāvādidoṣadhvaṃsādbhaveddvijaḥ vasuvedākhyasaṃskārapūrṇa itthaṃ dvijaḥ sthitaḥ

plain_english: Conception, male-producing, parting, birth, naming, exit, food tasting, tonsure, and the eighth.
sanskrit_cite: garbhādhānaṃ puṃsavanaṃ sīmanto jātakarma ca nāma niṣkrāmaṇaṃ cānnapraśaścūḍā tathāṣṭamī

plain_english: In vow binding and sacrificial, sacred thread and worldly rites, in order: soma-related, cow gift, veda-moon purification, from celibacy.
sanskrit_cite: vratabandhaiṣṭike maujjībhautike saumikaṃ kramāt godānamiti vedendusaṃskriyā brahmacaryataḥ

plain_english: Marriage is fifteenth; from there seven cooked sacrifices, eighth-day rites, fortnightly, ancestral offering, and the shravana-agrayana pair.
sanskrit_cite: pratyudvāhaḥ pañcadaśaḥ sapta pākamakhāstvataḥ aṣṭakāḥ pārvaṇī śrāddhaṃ śrāvaṇyāgrāyaṇīdvayam

plain_english: Chaitra and ashvayuja; after them seven oblation sacrifices; placed fire offering, full moon, and seeing.
sanskrit_cite: caitrī cāśvayujī paścāt saptaiva tu havirmakhāḥ ādheyamagnihotraṃ ca paurṇamāsaḥ sadarśakaḥ

plain_english: Four-month rite, animal binding, with sautramani; these, agnishtoma first, then soma-related and sixteen vajapeya.
sanskrit_cite: cāturmāsyaṃ paśūdbandhaḥ sautrāmaṇyā saha tvamī agniṣṭomo@tipūrvo@tha sokyyaḥ ṣoḍaśivājapau

plain_english: Aptoryama and atiratra; these seven are soma-established; golden-foot sacrifice surrounded by a thousand.
sanskrit_cite: āptoryāmātirātrau ca saptaitāḥ somasaṃsthitāḥ hiraṇyapādādimakhaḥ sahasreṇa samāvṛtaḥ

plain_english: The thirty-eighth is horse sacrifice; householder rite would be by measure; forest and renunciation rites are considered the fortieth.
sanskrit_cite: aṣṭatriṃśastvaśvamedho gārhasthyamiyatā bhavet vānasthyapārivrājye ca catvāriṃśadamī matāḥ

plain_english: Compassion, forbearance, non-envy, purity, good conduct, auspiciousness, non-miserliness, and non-desire are remembered as this eightfold set of qualities of the self.
sanskrit_cite: dayā kṣamānasūyā ca śuddhiḥ satkṛtimaṅgale akārpaṇyāspṛhe cātmaguṇāṣṭakamidaṃ smṛtam

plain_english: The girdle, staff, skin, lifelong observances, fire worship, twilight rite, and alms are the seven consecrations, and there are also seven vows.
sanskrit_cite: mekhalā daṇḍamajinatryāyuṣe vahnyupāsanam saṃdhyā bhikṣeti saṃskārāḥ sapta sapta vratāni ca

plain_english: The Bhauta and Pashupata are two, then the Ganesha and Ganapatya, and with the Unmattaka, sword-edge, and Ghrita-lord observances they make fourteen in all.
sanskrit_cite: bhauteśapāśupatye dve gāṇeśaṃ gāṇapatyakam unmattakāsidhārākhyaghṛteśāni caturdaśa

plain_english: These are remembered as the principal consecrations of vow-binding; in the case of renunciation, the final rite is as if in the womb, and by that one is consecrated.
sanskrit_cite: ete tu vratabandhasya saṃskārā aṅginaḥ smṛtāḥ pārivrājyasya garbhe syādantyeṣṭiriti saṃskṛtaḥ

plain_english: Then the person becomes twice-born and fit to attain a share in Rudra; the guru should apply these consecrations in the very sequence of the breath.
sanskrit_cite: dvijo bhavettato yogyo rudrāṃśāpādanāya saḥ etānprāṇakrameṇaiva saṃskārānyojayedguruḥ

plain_english: Alternatively, using oblations of sesame and the like preceded by mantra, one uses the formula: Om, the heart, the name, 'I purify, beloved of fire'.
sanskrit_cite: athavāhutiyogena tilādyairmantrapūrvakaiḥ praṇavo hṛdayaṃ nāma śodhayāmyagnivallabhā

plain_english: Thus, in sequence, with the head and other limbs, again and again: because the twice-born state is truly of the nature of consciousness, characterized by peace and the rest.
sanskrit_cite: evaṃ krameṇa mūrdhādyairaṅgairatatpunaḥ punaḥ yataściddharma evāsau śāntyādyātmā dvijanmatā

plain_english: Therefore awareness arises in the state of Rudra through that very sequence, just as gold and other metals, in refining, are transformed by the force of sequence.
sanskrit_cite: tena rudratayā saṃvittatkrameṇaiva jāyate yathā hemādidhātūnāṃ pāke kramavaśādbhavet

plain_english: Likewise, as with silver and the rest, in the consecration of awareness within the twice-born state the womb is not the cause; there, one who is of peaceful nature is called twice-born.
sanskrit_cite: rajatādi tathā saṃvitsaṃskāre dvijatāntare yonirna kāraṇaṃ tatra śāntātmā dvija ucyate

plain_english: This has been examined by the sage in the Moksha-dharma and elsewhere, and it has also been ascertained by the Lord in scriptures such as the Mukuta.
sanskrit_cite: muninā mokṣadharmādāvetacca pravivecitam mukuṭādiṣu śāstreṣu devenāpi nirūpitam

plain_english: Because awareness can arise similarly through similar bodily connection, from the standpoint of common convention, in the Smarta sense the son of two twice-born parents is called twice-born.
sanskrit_cite: saṃvido dehasaṃbhedātsadṛśātsadṛśodayāt bhūmābhiprāyataḥ smārte dvijanmā dvijayoḥ sutaḥ

plain_english: Even seers born of mothers associated with low-caste conditions of mind, speech, or birth had elevated minds; what need, then, of brahminhood alone to be a worthy receptacle?
sanskrit_cite: antyajātīyadhīvādijananījanmalābhataḥ utkṛṣṭacittā ṛṣayaḥ kiṃ brāhmaṇyena bhājanam

plain_english: For this reason, in this secret scripture that teaches the truth of real meaning, conduct based on birth and similar factors is indeed taught for the Śāmbhava path.
sanskrit_cite: ata evārthasattattvadeśinyasminna diśyate rahasyaśāstre jātyādisamācāro hi śāmbhave

plain_english: But the pāśava scriptures are thoroughly of the nature of vāma-śakti, serving accomplishment in creation and related aims, and also serving fear and the arrangement of results under Śambhu.
sanskrit_cite: pāśavāni tu śāstrāṇi vāmaśaktyātmakānyalam sṛṣṭyāṃcisiddhaye śaṃbhoḥ śaṅkātatphalakḷptaye

plain_english: For one who has been made twice-born, descent from the twelve-end comes not merely by touch, but by resting in union with one's own self and suddenly descending.
sanskrit_cite: āpāditadvijatvasya dvādaśānte nijaikyataḥ sparśamātrānna viśrāntyā jhaṭityevāvarohataḥ

plain_english: By the conferring of a Rudra-share, the samaya-initiate becomes consecrated and is thereby fit for study, hearing, daily worship, and service to the guru.
sanskrit_cite: rudrāṃśāpādanaṃ yena samayī saṃskṛto bhavet adhītau śravaṇe nityaṃ pūjāyāṃ gurusevane

plain_english: One authorized as a samaya-initiate should worship the Lord under the guru, and the guru should make that person, now given a Rudra-share, hear the samaya-pledges.
sanskrit_cite: samayyadhikṛto@nyatra guruṇā vibhumarcayet tamāpāditarudrāṃśaṃ samayān śrāvayedguruḥ

plain_english: In the Yāmala and related texts of the Goddess, the pledges are set forth as eight groups of eight, including restraint in speech and action, concealment, worship, satiation, and contemplation.
sanskrit_cite: aṣṭāṣṭakātmakāndevyāyāmalādau nirūpitān avādo@karaṇaṃ gūḍhiḥ pūjā tarpaṇabhāvane

plain_english: Striking and deluding, and so on, belong to an eightfold set of pledges expressed in eight ways, forming the unified samaya conduct that reflects the nature of mantra and tantra.
sanskrit_cite: hananaṃ mohanaṃ ceti samayāṣṭakamaṣṭadhā svabhāvaṃ mantratantrāṇāṃ samayācāramelakam

plain_english: One should not speak false, harsh, or untrue words, nor engage in fruitless action, harm, or touching another's wife.
sanskrit_cite: asatpralāpaṃ paruṣamanṛtaṃ nāṣṭadhā vadet aphalaṃ ceṣṭitaṃ hiṃsāṃ paradārābhimarśanam

plain_english: One should not practice pride, hypocrisy, or rites for spirits, poison, and disease, and one should guard one's own mantra, rosary, and knowledge that has the nature of true knowledge.
sanskrit_cite: garvaṃ dambhaṃ bhūtaviṣavyādhitantraṃ nacācaret svaṃ mantramakṣasūtraṃ ca vidyāṃ jñānasvarūpakam

plain_english: One should conceal one's conduct, qualities, hardships, and signs of success, and one should honor the guru, the scripture, the god, the fire, elders in knowledge, women, and the vow.
sanskrit_cite: samācārānguṇānkleśānsiddhiliṅgāni gūhayet guruṃ śāstraṃ devavahnī jñānavṛddhāṃstriyo vratam

plain_english: According to one's ability, one should worship the guru-lineage and this eightfold group: the poor, the afflicted, ancestors, field-guardians, living beings, and birds.
sanskrit_cite: guruvargaṃ yathāśaktyā pūjayedaṣṭakaṃ tvidam dīnānkliṣṭānpitṝnkṣetrapālānprāṇigaṇān khagān

plain_english: One should satiate the cremation-ground host of beings, the goddess of the body, Śiva, Śakti, and likewise the self, as well as the seal that has the form of mantra.
sanskrit_cite: śmāśānikaṃ bhūtagaṇaṃ dehadevīśca tarpayet śivaṃ śaktiṃ tathātmānaṃ mudrāṃ mantrasvarūpakam

plain_english: One should contemplate worldly enjoyment and liberation as taught by the guru, and restrain attachment, hatred, envy, contraction, jealousy, and pride.
sanskrit_cite: saṃsārabhuktimuktīśca guruvaktrāttu bhāvayet rāgaṃ dveṣamasūyāṃ ca saṃkocerṣyābhimānitāḥ

plain_english: One should strike down those who break the pledges and their wrong practices, as well as the cruel and hostile followers of the bound path, slanderers, and dullards.
sanskrit_cite: samayapratibhettṝṃstadanācārāṃśca ghātayet paśumārgasthitānkrūrāndveṣiṇaḥ piśunāñjaḍān

plain_english: One should delude the king's evil attendants and those who create obstacles, and one should worship the shakinis, who are described in this way in the revered scripture.
sanskrit_cite: rājñaścānucarānpāpānvighnakartṝṃśca mohayet śākinyaḥ pūjanīyāśca tāścetthaṃ śrīgamoditāḥ

plain_english: The shakinis have twofold boldness, fourfold desire, and eightfold greed; therefore they are to be feared. That is enough to say.
sanskrit_cite: sāhasaṃ dviguṇaṃ yāsāṃ kāmaścaiva caturguṇaḥ lobhaścāṣṭaguṇastāsāṃ śaṅkyaṃ śākinya ityalam

plain_english: Those who claim to stand in the kula tradition but remain outside the heroic substances should not be lived with; the revered Madhava Kula says one must not dwell together with such bound ones.
sanskrit_cite: kulāmnāyasthitā vīradravyabāhyāstu ye na taiḥ paśubhiḥ saha vastavyamiti śrīmādhave kule

plain_english: One should always worship the circle of deities, the guru, the fire, and the scripture as equal, and should not eat anything at all that has not first been offered to them.
sanskrit_cite: devatācakragurvagniśāstraṃ sāmyātsadārcayet aniveditametebhyo na kiṃcidapi bhakṣayet

plain_english: One should not take the guru's property and should honor the guru's circle; that circle is to be regarded, through knowledge, as like his brother, wife, and children.
sanskrit_cite: etaddravyaṃ nāpaharedguruvargaṃ prapūjayet sa ca tadbhrātṛbhāryātukprāyo vidyākṛto bhavet

plain_english: That relation is not based on birth or worldly ties, for such a person remains bound; instead, one's attachment should serve the accomplishment of worship of the guru.
sanskrit_cite: na yonisaṃbandhakṛto laukikaḥ sa paśuryataḥ tasyābhiṣvaṅgabhūmistu gurvārādhanasiddhaye

plain_english: The guru's group should not be worshipped for its own greatness but honored like the guru; one must not criticize the guru or give any reason for such criticism.
sanskrit_cite: arcyo na svamahimnā tu tadvargo guruvatpunaḥ gurornindāṃ na kurvīta tasyai hetuṃ nacācaret

plain_english: One should not listen to criticism of the guru, should not anger him, and should not do anything in his presence without permission, except serving him.
sanskrit_cite: naca tāṃ śṛṇuyānnainaṃ kopayennāgrato@sya ca vinājñayā prakurvīta kiṃcittatsevanādṛte

plain_english: Worldly and non-worldly duties, anger, play, austerity, recitation, and anything used by the guru—such as his bed, clothes, or seat—are all subject to strict restraint.
sanskrit_cite: laukikālaukikaṃ kṛtyaṃ krodhaṃ krīḍāṃ tapo japam gurūpabhuktaṃ yatkiṃcicchayyāvastrāsanādikam

plain_english: One should not use what the guru has used and should not touch it with the feet; instead one should honor it. The revered Traishirasa says that violations call for expiations such as krcchra and candrayana.
sanskrit_cite: nopabhuñjīta tatpadbhyāṃ na spṛśetkiṃtu vandayet śrīmattraiśirase@pyuktaṃ kṛcchracāndrāyaṇādibhiḥ

plain_english: Even if someone stands in the forest like a log, follows the razor-edge vow, and is firmly established in restraints and observances, he still does not attain the supreme state.
sanskrit_cite: araṇye kāṣṭhavattiṣṭhedasidhārāvrato@pi san niyamastho yamastho@pi tatpadaṃ nāśnute param

plain_english: But one who is devoted to worship of the guru in thought, action, and speech obtains from the pleased guru the full and greatly wondrous highest good.
sanskrit_cite: gurvārādhanasaktastu manasā karmaṇā girā prāpnoti gurutastuṣṭāt pūrṇaṃ śreyo mahādbhutam

plain_english: Just as the earth, covered on all sides by falling snow, becomes hard like stone through contact with the wind and remains so, so too a certain state becomes fixed.
sanskrit_cite: himapātairyathā bhūmiśchāditā sā samantataḥ mārutaśleṣasaṃyogādaśmavattiṣṭhate sadā

plain_english: In restraints and the like, when one becomes immobile, only a limited state is grasped, like that hardened snow; but from a properly worshipped guru one obtains full, expanding knowledge.
sanskrit_cite: yamādau niścale tadvadbhāva ekastu gṛhyate gurostvārādhitātpūrṇaṃ prasarajjñānamāpyate

plain_english: Consciousness is present everywhere and abides in the knowable; the teaching of one who knows this can immediately lift one upward. Therefore one should worship the guru.
sanskrit_cite: sarvato@vasthitaṃ cittvaṃ jñeyasthaṃ yasya tatkathā sadya eva nayedūrdhvaṃ tasmādārādhayedgurum

plain_english: The revered Sara says that even conversation with such a guru destroys sin in an instant; therefore one should examine a guru carefully, using scriptural teaching and the signs of true knowledge.
sanskrit_cite: śrīsāre@pyasya saṃbhāṣātpātakaṃ naśyati kṣaṇāt tasmātparīkṣya yatnena śāstroktyā jñānalakṣaṇaiḥ

plain_english: Live according to scriptural conduct and associate with the guru in that way. He may sometimes teach out of affection, but he cannot be won over by greed.
sanskrit_cite: śāstrācāreṇa varteta tena saṅgaṃ tathā kuru snehājjātu vadejjñānaṃ lobhānna hriyate hi saḥ

plain_english: When the guru is pleased, the gods and ancestors are satisfied; beings cross beyond the hells and go immediately to the great city of Shiva.
sanskrit_cite: tena tuṣṭena tṛpyanti devāḥ pitara evaca uttīrya narakādyānti sadyaḥ śivapuraṃ mahat

plain_english: The house where the guru eats or stays is said to reach Shiva's city; knowing this, one should always worship one's own guru in the ancestral shraddha rite.
sanskrit_cite: bhuṅkte tiṣṭhedyatra gṛhe vrajecchivapuraṃ tu saḥ iti jñātvā sadā pitrye śrāddhe svaṃ gurumarcayet

plain_english: The guru himself should eat and direct others for that purpose; an initiated disciple should not perform the shraddha and similar rites independently.
sanskrit_cite: bhuñjīta sa svayaṃ cānyānādiśettatkṛte guruḥ yo dīkṣitastu śrāddhādau svatantraṃ vidhimācaret

plain_english: If he acts independently, everything becomes fruitless and the pledge is transgressed; one should also avoid substances offered in the Saiddhantika way or fit for Chandi.
sanskrit_cite: tasya tanniṣphalaṃ sarvaṃ samayena ca laṅghyate saiddhāntikārpitaṃ caṇḍīyogyaṃ dravyaṃ vivarjayet

plain_english: One should never utter a word that names a shakini; women are to be honored, even if they are unattractive, old, or earn their living by a craft.
sanskrit_cite: śākinīvācakaṃ śabdaṃ na kadācitsamuccaret striyaḥ pūjyā virūpāstu vṛddhāḥ śilpopajīvikāḥ

plain_english: Women of the lowest caste, women with deformed limbs, courtesans, and women who act freely are to be honored with effort, as declared in the revered scripture.
sanskrit_cite: antyā vikāritāṅgyaśca veśyāḥ svacchandaceṣṭitāḥ tathāca śrīgame proktaṃ pūjanīyāḥ prayatnataḥ

plain_english: They are without conventional conduct, eat all things, are beyond right and wrong, move by their own will, eat meat, and are unrestrained; they are like goddesses.
sanskrit_cite: nirācārāḥ sarvabhakṣyā dharmādharmavivarjitāḥ svacchandagāḥ palāśinyo lampaṭā devatā iva

plain_english: Courtesans and their houses are to be honored, and there one should worship the ritual sequence as at a sacred confluence; one must not do anything toward women that would make them feel disgust.
sanskrit_cite: veśyāḥ pūjyāstadgṛhaṃ ca prayāgo@tra yajetkramam strīṣu tannācaretkicidyena tābhyo jugupsate

plain_english: Therefore, one should not look at them naked or with breasts exposed; and even if an old woman is present, one should not feel disgust at her mudrikā.
sanskrit_cite: ato na nagnāstāḥ paśyennacāpi prakaṭastanīḥ vṛddhāyāḥ saṃsthitāyā vā na jugupseta mudrikām

plain_english: At the gathering one should not display deformity or beauty; one should worship an empty-bodied deity image at crossroads and similar places.
sanskrit_cite: vaikṛtyaṃ tatra saurūpyaṃ melakaṃ na prakāśayet devamūrtiṃ śūnyatanuṃ pūjayettripathādiṣu

plain_english: On all festivals, ordinary and special, worship should be performed; there is no break in observance toward the guru, and greed must be avoided in the gathering.
sanskrit_cite: sarvaparvasu sāmānyaviśeṣeṣu viśeṣataḥ pūjā guroranadhyāyo melake lobhavarjanam

plain_english: One should never feel disgust toward wine and other vīra substances, nor criticize them; rather, one should always honor those who partake of them.
sanskrit_cite: na jugupseta madyādi vīradravyaṃ kadācana na nindedatha vandeta nityaṃ tajjoṣiṇastathā

plain_english: For the sake of instruction, faults may be pointed out, but one must not hate in one's heart; instead, one should strive to uproot alien conceptions.
sanskrit_cite: upadeśāya na doṣā hṛdayaṃ cenna vidviṣet vijātīyavikalpāṃśotpuṃsanāya yateta ca

plain_english: The names of the guru, the scripture, and the goddesses should not be uttered casually in mantra outside of worship; when properly invoked, they should then be satisfied.
sanskrit_cite: guroḥ śāstrasya devīnāṃ nāma mantre yatastataḥ arcāto@nyatra noccāryamāhūtaṃ tarpayettataḥ

plain_english: One should not perform tarpaṇa for a mantra that has merely arrived, because it takes away half of one's body; so the Blessed Lord declared.
sanskrit_cite: āgatasya ca mantrasya na kuryāttarpaṇaṃ yadi haratyardhaśarīraṃ tadityūce bhagavānyataḥ

plain_english: In the revered Ūrmi scripture it is taught that one must not publicize the conduct of goddesses and vīras, must not feel disgust toward it, and must not speak without the ritual substance in hand.
sanskrit_cite: śrīmadūrmau ca devīnāṃ vīrāṇāṃ ceṣṭitaṃ na vai prathayenna jugupseta vadennādravyapāṇikaḥ

plain_english: One should speak the guru's name preceded by śrī, especially when holding an offering; one must not step over the shadow of the guru and other revered figures, and one must not associate with sectarian rivals.
sanskrit_cite: śrīpūrvaṃ nāma vaktavyaṃ gurordravyakareṇa ca gurvādīnāṃ na laṅghyā ca chāyā na tairthikaiḥ saha

plain_english: When talking, one may explain the meaning of one's own scripture, but should not speak otherwise or give hints. In an occasional rite, one should not add special worship beyond the daily worship.
sanskrit_cite: jalpaṃ kurvansvaśāstrārthaṃ vadennāpica sūcayet nityādviśeṣapūjāṃ ca kuryānnaimittike vidhau

plain_english: In the middle of the year, and especially during the pavitraka rite, one devoted to another mantra should not take part, and another scripture should not be followed.
sanskrit_cite: tato@pi madhye varṣasya tato@pi hi pavitrake anyastamantro nāsīta sevyaṃ śāstrāntaraṃ ca no

plain_english: Knowledge that is not firmly rooted can be shaken by the views of others. Household implements and weapons should be honored through fire and offering.
sanskrit_cite: aprarūḍhaṃ hi vijñānaṃ kampetetarabhāvanāt gṛhopaskaraṇāstrāṇi davatāyāgayogataḥ

plain_english: One should not touch or step over worshipful things with the feet. When the guru and his group come to the house, one should show them some special honor.
sanskrit_cite: arcyānīti na padbhyāṃ vai spṛśennāpi vilaṅghyet guruvarge gṛhāyāte viśeṣaṃ kaṃcidācaret

plain_english: One should not criticize initiated people out of hostility. If correction is given for instruction and without hostility, it is not a fault.
sanskrit_cite: dīkṣitānāṃ na nindādi kuryādvidveṣapūrvakam upadeśāya no doṣaḥ sa hyavidveṣapūrvakaḥ

plain_english: One should not live closely with those who hold lower views, such as Vaishnavas and others. One should not eat or sleep with them, nor reveal one's own spiritual state to them.
sanskrit_cite: na vaṣṇavādikādhaḥsthadṛṣṭibhiḥ saṃvasedalam sahabhojanaśayyādyarnaiṣāṃ prakaṭayetsthitim

plain_english: It is said in the revered Madhava lineage that one should always avoid Vedic and Vaishnava teachings, and whatever is spoken by those established in other systems.
sanskrit_cite: uktaṃ śrīṃmādhavakule śāsanāntarasaṃsthitān vedoktiṃ vaiṣṇavoktiṃ ca tairuktaṃ varjayetsadā

plain_english: Association with those of unworthy lineage brings the fear of falling from one's own lineage. Therefore, in the Kula tradition, especially where one vessel is shared, one should avoid them.
sanskrit_cite: akulīneṣu saṃparkāttatkulātpatanādbhayam ekapātre kulāmnāye tasmāttānparivarjayet

plain_english: If, through carelessness, one forms a friendship in a gathering with a follower of another Agama, the revered Urma teaches that one should worship the circle.
sanskrit_cite: pramādācca kṛte sakhye goṣṭhyāṃ cakraṃ tu pūjayet śrīmadūrmau ca kathitamāgamāntarasevake

plain_english: One should not associate at all with someone who delights in another guru, is deluded, lives off the property of the gods, harms the shakti, or is corrupt.
sanskrit_cite: gurvantararate mūḍhe devadravyopajīvake śaktihiṃsākare duṣṭe saṃparkaṃ naiva kārayet

plain_english: One should not go to a shrine or similar place in initiation and related matters out of mere doubt. If the prescribed faith has become weak, one should not act on that basis.
sanskrit_cite: na vikalpena dīkṣādau vrajedāyatanādikam uktāsthāśithilatve yannimittaṃ naiva taccaret

plain_english: One should not judge or speak of those in the teaching in terms of their former birth. One should deal with all simply as non-different from Shiva.
sanskrit_cite: śāsanasthānpurājātyā na paśyennāpyudīrayet naca vyavaharetsarvāñchivābhedena kevalam

plain_english: Sit with true knowledge, strive for illumination, and do not fall into uninitiated fruitlessness.
sanskrit_cite: sadvidyaiḥ sākamāsīta jñānadīptyai yateta ca nāsaṃskṛtāṃ vrajettajjaṃ viphalatvaṃ nacānayet

plain_english: Night practice in the assembly center excludes ordinary people, and the devotee of the goddess does not smell burning meat.
sanskrit_cite: melakārdhaniśācaryā janavarjaṃ ca tannahi māṃsādidāhagandhaṃ ca jighreddevīpriyo hyasau

plain_english: Protecting the guru's command, one abandons mantra-identification and becomes equipped with scripture, worship, japa, meditation, and discernment.
sanskrit_cite: gurvājñāṃ pālayansarvaṃ tyajenmantramayo bhavet śāstrapūjājapadhyānavivekatadupakriyāḥ

plain_english: Do not perform fruitless action, do not strive in threefold action, do not dispute through mantra and tantra, and do not eat poison.
sanskrit_cite: akurvanniṣphalāṃ naiva ceṣṭeta trividhāṃ kriyām mantratantrairna vādaṃ ca kuryānno bhakṣayedviṣam

plain_english: When pledges are breached, ask the guru in his presence, or another of his lineage in his absence.
sanskrit_cite: samayānāṃ vilope ca guruṃ pṛcchedasannidhau tadvargaṃ nijasantānamanyaṃ tasyāpyasaṃnidhau

plain_english: Follow what he said without doubt and with effort, because the mind has been made one with scriptural awakening.
sanskrit_cite: tenoktamanutiṣṭhecca nirvikalpaṃ prayatnataḥ yataḥ śāstrādisaṃbodhatanmayīkṛtamānasaḥ

plain_english: Shiva indeed is the guru; his word is truth, and humility toward the guru again serves Shiva's self-purification.
sanskrit_cite: śiva eva gururnāsya vāgasatyā viniḥsaret śivasya svātmasaṃskṛtyai prahvībhāvo guroḥ punaḥ

plain_english: His satisfaction gives fruit to the disciple, since attainment depends on the guru, even in samaya, for the knowledge-bearer.
sanskrit_cite: hlādāyetyubhayārthāya tattuṣṭiḥ phaladā śiśoḥ gurvāyattaikasiddhirhisamayyapi vibodhabhāk

plain_english: By great regard for that knowledge one knows the supreme guru; therefore, having obtained knowledge, one does not rely on external men.
sanskrit_cite: tadbodhabahumānena vidyādgurutamaṃ gurum ataḥ saṃprāpya vijñānaṃ yo gurau bāhyamānavān

plain_english: He is not trusted in knowledge; indeed he is fallen, and a mind not trusted in knowledge is not established by mere words.
sanskrit_cite: nāsau vijñānaviśvasto nāsatyaṃ bhraṣṭa eva saḥ jñānānāśvastacittaṃ taṃ vacomātreṇa śāstritam

plain_english: Never worship a knowledge-corrupter with the heart; such a person is not a guru, and even if made one, he should be abandoned.
sanskrit_cite: bhaktaṃ ca nārcayejjātu hṛdā vijñānadūṣakam tādṛk ca na guruḥ kāryastaṃ kṛtvāpi parityajet

plain_english: With primary intellect one does not regard gurus among Vaishnavas and others as gurus; thus a qualification is stated in the named scripture.
sanskrit_cite: mukhyabuddhyā na saṃpaśyedvaiṣṇavādigatāngurūn tathāca śrīmadūrmyākhye guroruktaṃ viśeṣaṇam

plain_english: The guru's command is not to be neglected in a life doubt; Kaula initiation and Kaula scripture reveal truth knowledge.
sanskrit_cite: gurvājñā prāṇasaṃdehe nopekṣyā no vikalpyate kauladīkṣā kaulaśāstraṃ tattvajñānaṃ prakāśitam

plain_english: He by whom one is truly called guru is the guru; others are mere name-bearers, as the scripture states the qualification.
sanskrit_cite: yenāsau gururityukto hyanye vai nāmadhāriṇaḥ śrīmadānandaśāstre ca tathaivoktaṃ viśeṣaṇam

plain_english: Because initiation gives mantra scripture and truth knowledge, he is indeed the guru; the unmanifest linga stands, and no linga is held.
sanskrit_cite: yasmāddīkṣā mantraśāstraṃ tattvajñānaṃ sa vai guruḥ tiṣṭhedavyaktaliṅgaśca na liṅgaṃ dhārayet kvacit

plain_english: One should not equally mix conduct with linga-bearers; only the linga-bearer is to be protected, not treated with disgust, even if deformed.
sanskrit_cite: na liṅgibhiḥ samaṃ kaiścitkuryādācāramelanam kevalaṃ liṅginaḥ pālyā na bībhatsyā virūpakāḥ

plain_english: In the Kula it is said that liberation comes from removing doubt; this impure dwelling and even news of liberation are rare.
sanskrit_cite: śrīmadrātrikule coktaṃ mokṣaḥ śaṅkāpahānitaḥ aśuddhavāsasnayaiṣā mokṣavārtāpi durlabhā

plain_english: Do not write the mantra heart; extract the mantra from its limb, but do not scratch it in writing.
sanskrit_cite: na likhenmantrahṛdayaṃ śrīmanmāloditaṃ kila tadaṅgāduddharenmantraṃ natu lekhe vilekhayet

plain_english: Do not fixate on non-truth, and do not act from partiality toward knowers of birth, knowledge, family, conduct, body, place, quality, or meaning.
sanskrit_cite: atattve@bhiniveśaṃ ca na kuryātpakṣapātataḥ jātividyākulācāradehadeśaguṇārthajān

plain_english: Quickly abandon the eight planets and non-planets shown in the cave, and likewise those shown as horse in the Nishichara beginning.
sanskrit_cite: grahāngrahānivāṣṭau drāktyajedgahvararśitān tathā śrīniśicārādau hayatvenopadarśitān

plain_english: If I am a Brahmin, how can this birth-planet, which obstructs others, be performed beyond what Veda scripture says?
sanskrit_cite: brāhmaṇo@haṃ mayā vedaśāstroktādaparaṃ katham anuṣṭheyamayaṃ jātigrahaḥ paranirodhakaḥ

plain_english: Thus others are also examples; by the Kula cave path, even the unwilling shows that form in non-that nature.
sanskrit_cite: evamanye@pyudāhāryāḥ kulagahvaravartmanā atatsvabhāve tādrūpyaṃ darśayannavaśe@pi yaḥ

plain_english: He here covers true form, like a planet as said; in the nature of consciousness there is no conception of birth and the like.
sanskrit_cite: svarūpācchādakaḥ so@tra graho graha ivoditaḥ saṃvitsvabhāve no jātiprabhṛtiḥ kāpi kalpanā

plain_english: Form covers that form by true form; any conception sufficiently covers the indivisible self of the consciousness principle.
sanskrit_cite: rūpaṃ sā tvasvarūpeṇa tadrūpaṃ chādayatyalam yā kācitkalpanā saṃvittattvasyākhaṇḍitātmanaḥ

plain_english: The supreme lord declared in the splendid Ananda scripture that all should abandon the contraction-causing graha-state.
sanskrit_cite: saṃkocakāriṇī sarvaḥ sa grahastāṃ parityajet śrīmadānandaśāstre ca kathitaṃ parameṣṭhinā

plain_english: There the independent lord Vama is not caused by purity; goddess satisfaction in sacrifice is not from blood, flesh, or purity arrangement.
sanskrit_cite: nirapekṣaḥ prabhurvāmo na śuddhyā tatra kāraṇam devītṛptirmakhe raktamāṃsairno śaucayojanāt

plain_english: Discussion should be done equally with twice-born and outcastes; even at its end, rays unchanged by that maker would arise from doubt as hell.
sanskrit_cite: dvijāntyajaiḥ samaṃ kāryā carcānte@pi marīcayaḥ avikārakṛtastena vikalpānnirayo bhavet

plain_english: The body is all-god-filled in all beings; this is clearly determined by splendid Nakulesha and others.
sanskrit_cite: sarvadevamayaḥ kāyaḥ sarvaprāṇiṣviti sphuṭam śrīmadbhirnakuleśādyairapyetatsunirūpitam

plain_english: The body itself is the shrine, not another; one should go to one tirtha, remember the mantra, and avoid other tirthas.
sanskrit_cite: śarīramevāyatanaṃ nānyadāyatanaṃ vrajet tīrthamekaṃ smarenmantramanyatīrthāni varjayet

plain_english: Having easily known this rite, one should abandon the rite-net; samadhi certainty is not obtained by another.
sanskrit_cite: vidhimenaṃ sukhaṃ jñātvā vidhijālaṃ parityajet samādhirniścayaṃ muktvā na cānyenopalabhyate

plain_english: Thus thinking, the rite-knower should avoid delusion; besides the heart of the mantra, nothing else is supreme anywhere.
sanskrit_cite: iti matvā vidhānajñaḥ saṃmohaṃ parivarjayet mantrasya hṛdayaṃ muktvā na cānyatparamaṃ kvacit

plain_english: Thus thinking, the rite-knower should abandon the mantra-net; he should feed the offering and throw the river remainder in water.
sanskrit_cite: iti matvā vidhānajño mantrajālaṃ parityajet naivedyaṃ prāśayennadyāstaccheṣaṃ ca jale kṣipet

plain_english: When eaten by them, no fault would arise; water-born and previously initiated ones are protected by supremacy from contact.
sanskrit_cite: tairbhukte na bhaveddoṣo jalajaiḥ pūrvadīkṣitaiḥ avayaśpālanīyatvātparattvena saṃgamāt

plain_english: These pledges are declared as means of knowledge attainment; thus proclaiming pledges, the teacher worships the god.
sanskrit_cite: jñānaprāptyabhyupāyatvātsamayāste prakīrtitāḥ evaṃ saṃśrāvya samayāndevaṃ saṃpūjya daiśikaḥ

plain_english: He should release in his own consciousness space, peaceful, from form dissolution; if his son initiation is not to be done immediately.
sanskrit_cite: visarjayetsvacidvyomni śānte mūrtivilāpanāt yadi putrakadīkṣāsya na kāryā samanantaram

plain_english: Then he should anoint that child and himself with the Shiva pot by scripture, because water-form is the great lord.
sanskrit_cite: tadābhiṣiñcetsāstreṇa śivakumbhena taṃ śiśum ātmānaṃ ca tato yasmājjalamūrtirmaheśvaraḥ

plain_english: Mantra-uniting all-nourishing anointing should be done; this samaya initiation is revealed from detail and brevity.
sanskrit_cite: mantrayuṅnikhilāpyāyī kāryaṃ tadabhiṣecanam iti samayadīkṣaṇamidaṃ prakāśitaṃ vistarācca saṃkṣepāt
